title: 563. Peter the Great: Bloodbath in the Kremlin (Part 2)

sentences.en: The Tsar is a man of very hot temper, soon inflamed, and very brutal in his passion.
sentences.zh: 沙皇脾气非常暴躁，一点就着，发起火来极其残暴。

sentences.en: He raises his natural heat by drinking much brandy, which he rectified himself with great application.
sentences.zh: 他通过喝烈酒来提升体内的燥热，这些酒都是他自己非常刻苦地蒸馏出来的。

sentences.en: He is subject to convulsive motions all over his body, and his head seems to be afflicted with these.
sentences.zh: 他的全身都会不由自主地抽搐，头部似乎也备受这种抽搐的折磨。

sentences.en: He was desirous to understand our doctrine.
sentences.zh: 他很想了解我们的教义。

sentences.en: He was indeed resolved to encourage learning, and to polish his people by sending some of them to travel in other countries, and to draw strangers to come and live among them.
sentences.zh: 他的确下定决心要振兴学术，通过派遣一些人去其他国家游历来教化他的国民，并吸引外国人在他们中间定居。

sentences.en: He seemed apprehensive still of his sister's intrigues.
sentences.zh: 他似乎依然对姐姐的阴谋感到担忧。

sentences.en: After I had seen him often, and had conversed much with him, I could not but adore the depth of the providence of God,
sentences.zh: 在经常见到他并与他深入交谈之后，我不得不赞叹上帝天意的深邃，

sentences.en: that had raised up such a furious man to so absolute authority over so great a part of the world.
sentences.zh: 竟然让这样一个狂暴的人掌握了对世界上如此广袤土地的绝对统治权。

sentences.en: So there we have a Scotsman, Dominic, as you could tell from my magnificent impression of a Scotsman.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有个苏格兰人，多米尼克，正如你从我那模仿苏格兰人的精妙神态中听出来的那样。

sentences.en: A man called Gilbert Burnett, who met with Peter the Great in London in 1698.
sentences.zh: 一个叫吉尔伯特·伯内特的人，他于1698年在伦敦见到了彼得大帝。

sentences.en: But by far the most significant and interesting thing about Gilbert Burnett is that he was the Bishop of Salisbury.
sentences.zh: 但关于吉尔伯特·伯内特，迄今为止最重要、最有趣的事情是，他曾是索尔兹伯里的主教。

sentences.en: He was.
sentences.zh: 他确实是。

sentences.en: And how wonderful it is, we are doing this series about Peter the Great, who we left as a master of Moscow.
sentences.zh: 这多么奇妙啊，我们正在制作关于彼得大帝的系列节目，而我们上期说到他已经成为了莫斯科的主人。

sentences.en: He'd crushed his sister Sophia's resistance.
sentences.zh: 他粉碎了他姐姐索菲亚的抵抗。

sentences.en: He'd secured the loyalty of the streltsy, these, frankly, sinister and faintly grotesque soldiers who wear yellow boots and caftans,
sentences.zh: 他确保了射击军的忠诚，说实话，这群士兵显得阴森诡异，穿着黄色靴子和卡夫坦长袍，

sentences.en: and who have a great fondness for jumping on the body parts of people that they've chopped and sliced into little bits.
sentences.zh: 并且极其喜欢踩踏那些被他们砍成碎块的人的身体部位。

sentences.en: But here he is in England, he's twitching uncontrollably, he's drinking brandy, he's chatting about Protestant doctrine,
sentences.zh: 但现在他来到了英国，他不受控制地抽搐着，喝着白兰地，聊着新教教义，

sentences.en: and he's doing it with a man from my neck of the woods, from Wiltshire, from Salisbury.
sentences.zh: 而且他是和来自我老家那个地方的人——来自威尔特郡，来自索尔兹伯里的人——在聊这些。

sentences.en: From the Salisbury area?
sentences.zh: 来自索尔兹伯里地区？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's great to have Wiltshire in the Salisbury area on the show.
sentences.zh: 我是说，节目能把威尔特郡和索尔兹伯里地区囊括进来，真的很棒。

sentences.en: Dominic, I'll be honest, my worry when you suggested doing Peter the Great was that Salisbury wouldn't get a look in, but how wrong I was.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，说实话，当你建议做彼得大帝这一期时，我担心的就是索尔兹伯里不会出场，但我错得太离谱了。

sentences.en: The weirdest thing is not just that he's chatting about Christian doctrine with people from the Salisbury area, it's the fact that he's doing it under a false name.
sentences.zh: 最诡异的事情不仅在于他跟索尔兹伯里地区的人聊基督教教义，而在于他是用假名在进行这一切。

sentences.en: So he's travelled incognito.
sentences.zh: 所以他是隐姓埋名去旅行的。

sentences.en: I mean, this is such a mad story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个如此疯狂的故事。

sentences.en: The Tsar of all the Russians has basically taken an extended gap year to travel anonymously to Western Europe,
sentences.zh: 全俄罗斯的沙皇基本上给自己放了个超长间隔年，匿名去西欧旅行，

sentences.en: and to hang around in shipyards and in taverns, interfering with actresses, and kind of behaving in ludicrous ways, wheelbarrow races.
sentences.zh: 在造船厂和酒馆里闲逛，打扰女演员，做出各种荒谬的行为，比如玩独轮车比赛。

sentences.en: We both love a wheelbarrow race.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都很喜欢独轮车比赛。

sentences.en: We've only told their story 20 times on The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 我们在《历史的余烬》里已经讲过他们20次故事了。

sentences.en: And now we're going to tell us again.
sentences.zh: 现在我们又要再讲一次了。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So, shall we get back to where we left off?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们回到上期结束的地方继续讲好吗？

sentences.en: So, the summer of 1689, Peter has deposed Sophia.
sentences.zh: 话说1689年夏天，彼得废黜了索菲亚。

sentences.en: He's 17 years old.
sentences.zh: 他当时17岁。

sentences.en: He is now, we haven't actually described him physically.
sentences.zh: 他现在——我们其实还没描述过他的外貌。

sentences.en: He is a massive bloke.
sentences.zh: 他是个身材高大的壮汉。

sentences.en: He's six foot seven.
sentences.zh: 他身高六尺七（约2米）。

sentences.en: He's very kind of angular.
sentences.zh: 他的身形非常硬朗有棱角。

sentences.en: He's got long brown hair and he's got a moustache.
sentences.zh: 他留着长长的棕色头发，还留着八字胡。

sentences.en: Interesting, not a beard.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他没有留胡须。

sentences.en: Yeah, not a beard.
sentences.zh: 对，没有胡须。

sentences.en: Now, Bishop Burnett mentioned his convulsive motions.
sentences.zh: 现在，伯内特主教提到了他的抽搐动作。

sentences.en: So, some people say, well, maybe he's just very restless.
sentences.zh: 所以，有些人会说，嗯，也许他只是非常不安分。

sentences.en: He's very impatient and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他非常急躁之类的。

sentences.en: But other people say maybe he's got a kind of a nervous tick, because don't forget when he was 10 years old, he saw his family chopped up and stamped on.
sentences.zh: 但另一些人说，也许他有某种神经性抽搐，因为别忘了在他10岁的时候，他亲眼目睹了自己的家人被砍碎和践踏。

sentences.en: That would give you bad mental health, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 这会让你心理健康出问题，对吧？

sentences.en: I think BetterHelp or any mental health provider would have had a field day with Peter the Great, to be completely honest with you.
sentences.zh: 说句心里话，我觉得BetterHelp或者任何心理健康机构在彼得大帝身上绝对能赚得盆满钵满。

sentences.en: But I think it's also possible he's mildly epileptic.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得他可能有点轻微的癫痫。

sentences.en: There are lots of descriptions of him when he's in Europe, having sort of fits on the left-hand side of his face or his arm,
sentences.zh: 有很多关于他在欧洲时的描述，说他左半边脸或手臂会发生某种痉挛，

sentences.en: his eyes rolling back in his head, all of this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 双眼往上翻之类的种种表现。

sentences.en: And I think it's also fair to say, Tom, he doesn't have the best and healthiest lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得客观地讲，汤姆，他的生活方式可谈不上最好、最健康。

sentences.en: Because actually, although he's taken supreme power, he then sort of gives it away because he says to his mother,
sentences.zh: 因为事实上，尽管他夺取了最高权力，但他随后却把它放权了，因为他对母亲说，

sentences.en: you know, can you run Russia for me, please?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你能帮我管理一下俄罗斯吗？

sentences.en: Because I just want to hang around with my mates, with my soldiers.
sentences.zh: 因为我只想跟我的哥们儿、我的士兵们混在一起。

sentences.en: And his lathes.
sentences.zh: 还有他的车床。

sentences.en: And he wants to spend a lot of time, he loves the German suburb.
sentences.zh: 他想花大量时间——他极其热爱德国人聚居区。

sentences.en: So this place we talked about last time, which is full of kind of Scotsmen and Dutchmen and things.
sentences.zh: 就是我们上次聊过的那个地方，那里到处都是苏格兰人、荷兰人什么的。

sentences.en: And they're all smoking pipes outside Protestant churches and talking to women.
sentences.zh: 他们都在新教教堂外面抽着烟斗，跟女人们聊天。

sentences.en: Which the Orthodox Church doesn't approve of at all.
sentences.zh: 东正教对此是绝对无法容忍的。

sentences.en: Which the Orthodox Church doesn't approve of at all.
sentences.zh: 东正教对此是绝对无法容忍的。

sentences.en: And his closest friends, or some of them at least, come from the German suburb.
sentences.zh: 而他最亲密的朋友，至少其中一部分，就来自德国人聚居区。

sentences.en: So we talked last time, we promised we'd talk about General Gordon.
sentences.zh: 所以我们上次聊过，答应过要讲讲戈登将军。

sentences.en: We always liked General Gordon on the show.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目里一向很喜欢戈登将军。

sentences.en: So this is a different General Gordon, not the bloke who died in Khartoum.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个不同的戈登将军，不是死在喀土穆的那位仁兄。

sentences.en: But still a friend of the show.
sentences.zh: 但依然是节目的老朋友。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's a Scottish mercenary who came from the Highlands.
sentences.zh: 他是一个来自高地的苏格兰雇佣兵。

sentences.en: He came from a Catholic family.
sentences.zh: 他出身于一个天主教家庭。

sentences.en: So he basically left Scotland.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上离开了苏格兰。

sentences.en: And then he had an amazing career, actually.
sentences.zh: 然后他的职业生涯其实非常精彩。

sentences.en: He fought for the Swedes against the Poles.
sentences.zh: 他曾为瑞典人效力去攻打波兰人。

sentences.en: Then he fought for the Poles against the Swedes.
sentences.zh: 然后他又为波兰人效力去攻打瑞典人。

sentences.en: Then he fought for the Swedes against the Poles again.
sentences.zh: 接着他又为瑞典人效力再次攻打波兰人。

sentences.en: And then he fought for the Poles against the Swedes again.
sentences.zh: 然后他又为波兰人效力再次攻打瑞典人。

sentences.en: And that's fine, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很正常，对吧？

sentences.en: That's legitimate.
sentences.zh: 这是合法的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, nobody really minds about that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，其实没人介意这个。

sentences.en: That's how 17th century warfare works.
sentences.zh: 17世纪的战争就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: It's basically like being a star footballer.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就像当个球星一样。

sentences.en: You transfer from team to team.
sentences.zh: 你在不同的球队之间转会。

sentences.en: I think you can't fight against your own country, but you can fight for others.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你不能跟自己的国家作对，但你可以为其他人效力。

sentences.en: And that's completely legitimate.
sentences.zh: 这完全是合法的。

sentences.en: And he ended up serving the Tsars.
sentences.zh: 而他最终开始为沙皇效力。

sentences.en: And this guy, General Gordon, becomes basically Peter's chief military advisor.
sentences.zh: 这个叫戈登将军的家伙，基本上成了彼得的首席军事顾问。

sentences.en: His tutor, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想也可以算是他的导师。

sentences.en: And then there's another mercenary who is called Frantz Lefort, who's from Geneva, who basically is a massive drinker and a dancer, charming.
sentences.zh: 还有一个名叫弗兰茨·勒福特的雇佣兵，来自日内瓦，他基本上是个狂热的酒鬼和舞者，十分迷人。

sentences.en: His house, we're told, is always full of women, who Peter's biographer, Robert K.
sentences.zh: 据说他的家里总是挤满了女人，彼得的传记作家罗伯特·K·马西

sentences.en: Massey, describes as rollicking, buxom, sturdy wenches who did not take offense at barracks language or the admiring touch of rough male hands.
sentences.zh: 将她们描述为“喧闹、丰满、健壮的村姑，她们对军营粗话或粗糙男手的爱抚并不感到冒犯”。

sentences.en: So that kind of gives you a sense of the general vibe at these occasions.
sentences.zh: 所以这大概能让你感受到这些聚会上的总体氛围。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这么说很客观。

sentences.en: And just on the topic of rough male hands, Peter's hands are very calloused, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 顺便说到粗糙的男手这个话题，彼得的手上有很多老茧，对吧？

sentences.en: Because he's been with his lathes and all of that.
sentences.zh: 因为他一直在弄他的车床之类的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because he's been like chopping stones or whatever he's doing.
sentences.zh: 因为他一直在劈石头或者干别的什么活。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so when he goes on his gap year and he meets with all these members of royalty and stuff, he's always showing off his callouses.
sentences.zh: 所以当他去度间隔年并会见所有这些王室成员时，他总是喜欢炫耀他的老茧。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 他确实如此。

sentences.en: He's very proud of them.
sentences.zh: 他对此感到非常骄傲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: In an age when people would be proud of not having calloused hands, he's quite the reverse.
sentences.zh: 在一个以没有老茧为荣的时代，他却完全反其道而行之。

sentences.en: So over time, Peter and this bloke Lefort and their pals, so actually he picks up Lefort's girlfriend, who's called Anna Monge,
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，彼得和这个叫勒福特的家伙以及他们的同伴——事实上，他看上了勒福特的女友，名叫安娜·蒙斯，

sentences.en: and she loves a drink and a laugh and she becomes his mistress.
sentences.zh: 而她也喜欢喝酒和欢笑，并成为了他的情妇。

sentences.en: Anyway, Peter and all these pals, they basically, they form something that they call the Jolly Company.
sentences.zh: 总之，彼得和所有这些伙伴，他们基本上组建了一个自称为“欢乐连”的团体。

sentences.en: I feel, I don't actually think either of us would have really enjoyed life in the Jolly Company.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，其实我们俩谁都不会真正喜欢“欢乐连”里的生活。

sentences.en: I'd have hated it.
sentences.zh: 我会恨死它的。

sentences.en: I think you might enjoy it for a day.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你可能会喜欢一天吧。

sentences.en: It's basically a stag do, a massive stag do.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是一个单身派对，一个规模巨大的单身派对。

sentences.en: I hate stag do's.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌单身派对。

sentences.en: There's often about 80 of them, sometimes as many as 200.
sentences.zh: 他们通常有大约80人，有时甚至多达200人。

sentences.en: And remember, Peter is the Tsar of Russia and he's 17 years old.
sentences.zh: 而且别忘了，彼得是俄罗斯沙皇，而且他才17岁。

sentences.en: They will roam the land, basically turning up at Russian noblemen's houses and saying, you know, put us up.
sentences.zh: 他们会四处游荡，基本上是直接闯进俄罗斯贵族家里说，你知道的，给我们提供吃住。

sentences.en: And they'll have these enormous feasts.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会举行极其丰盛的宴宴。

sentences.en: The feast normally starts at midday.
sentences.zh: 宴会通常在中午开始。

sentences.en: It's actually very much like our working lunches at The Rest is History with the production team.
sentences.zh: 这其实非常像我们在《历史的余烬》节目组和制作团队的工作午餐。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: The feast starts at midday and it lasts till the next day.
sentences.zh: 宴会从中午开始，一直持续到第二天。

sentences.en: They have a pause every now and again to have a smoke or to play bowls or to shoot muskets or let off fireworks.
sentences.zh: 他们每隔一会儿就会暂停一下，抽根烟，打打地滚球，或者打火枪、放烟花。

sentences.en: And isn't this kind of shenanigans with bears and bellows and things?
sentences.zh: 还有用熊和风箱恶作剧之类的胡闹对吧？

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of beer drinking.
sentences.zh: 所以有大量的啤酒畅饮。

sentences.en: It's very like The Rest is History working lunches.
sentences.zh: 这真的很像《历史的余烬》的工作午餐。

sentences.en: There's a lot of beer drinking and toasts, but there's also pranks.
sentences.zh: 有大量的啤酒和干杯，但也有各种恶作剧。

sentences.en: We love a prank.
sentences.zh: 我们最喜欢恶作剧了。

sentences.en: So if there's a fat man there, they'll often strip the fat man and drag him across ice on his bare bottom.
sentences.zh: 所以如果现场有个胖子，他们通常会把这个胖子剥光衣服，然后让他光着屁股在冰面上被拖来拖去。

sentences.en: They would shove candles into you, insert candles and light them.
sentences.zh: 他们会把蜡烛塞进你体内，把蜡烛插进去然后点燃。

sentences.en: At least one man is killed by having air blown up him with bellows.
sentences.zh: 至少有一个人是用风箱往体内充气给活活弄死的。

sentences.en: So they insert bellows into him and blow you up.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把风箱插进他体内然后把你吹胀。

sentences.en: That's what I remember, the bellows, jape.
sentences.zh: 这就是我记忆中的风箱恶作剧。

sentences.en: Would you burst?
sentences.zh: 你会爆炸吗？

sentences.en: Do you think he burst?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他会爆炸吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不知道。

sentences.en: Because if they're playing japes on fat people, presumably if you blow a fat person up with a bellows, there's more capacity.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们是对胖子搞恶作剧，想必如果你用风箱把一个胖子吹胀，容量会更大一些。

sentences.en: I mean, Dominic, I've mentioned it before, but the brilliant evocation of all this,
sentences.zh: 我是说，多米尼克，我以前提过，但对这一切的精彩描绘——

sentences.en: the japes and the pranks and the frankly kind of murderous jollity of the jolly company is brilliantly evoked in The Great.
sentences.zh: 那些恶作剧、捉弄以及欢乐连那种坦率说带有杀戮色彩的狂欢，在《凯瑟琳大帝》里得到了精彩的呈现。

sentences.en: Right, the Catherine the Great series.
sentences.zh: 对，就是那个叶卡捷琳娜大帝系列剧。

sentences.en: With Nicholas Holt, who is playing Peter the Great's grandson, but I think he's actually playing Peter the Great in this.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉斯·霍尔特在里面饰演彼得大帝的孙子，但我认为他在这剧里其实演的就是彼得大帝本人。

sentences.en: Loads of toasts and going huzzah all the time.
sentences.zh: 有无数次干杯，大家一直在高喊乌拉（huzzah）。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is what's happening.
sentences.zh: 对，事情就是这样的。

sentences.en: Now, there is a slight, you could say there's a slight political side to this,
sentences.zh: 现在，这里面有一点，你可以说这具有某种政治色彩，

sentences.en: because we talked last time about how Peter loves to kind of do this role playing and quite subversive role playing.
sentences.zh: 因为我们上次聊过彼得是多么喜欢搞这种角色扮演，而且是非常具有颠覆性的角色扮演。

sentences.en: He loves giving people like fake titles and nicknames and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢给别人起诸如假头衔和绰号之类的东西。

sentences.en: So the jolly company have their own sort of what's called a mock czar, a guy who he calls the Prince Caesar, who's a friend of his called Fedor Romadonovsky.
sentences.zh: 所以“欢乐连”有他们自己的所谓“假沙皇”，一个被他称为“凯撒亲王”的家伙，那是他的一个朋友，名叫费多尔·罗莫达诺夫斯基。
zh_words: 费多尔·罗莫达诺夫斯基

sentences.en: And Peter calls him, your majesty.
sentences.zh: 而彼得称呼他为“陛下”。

sentences.en: When Peter writes a letter to him, he always signs himself, you know, I'm your slave, I'm your bondsman and stuff.
sentences.zh: 当彼得给他写信时，落款总是写着，你知道的，我是你的奴隶，我是你的臣民之类的。

sentences.en: And this guy Romadonovsky has to preside over the meetings of the jolly company.
sentences.zh: 而这个叫罗莫达诺夫斯基的家伙必须主持“欢乐连”的会议。

sentences.en: He almost pretends to be the czar, but he loves a prank.
sentences.zh: 他几乎是在假装自己是沙皇，但他特别喜欢恶作剧。

sentences.en: So his great prank, you would love this, Tom, if you turned up.
sentences.zh: 所以他的绝妙恶作剧——如果你去了的话，汤姆，你一定会喜欢这个。

sentences.en: When you arrive, especially if you're a kind of a newbie, you have to drink a large cup of peppered brandy that is offered to you by a trained bear.
sentences.zh: 当你到达时，特别是如果你是个新人的话，你必须喝下一大杯由一头受过训练的熊端给你的加了胡椒的白兰地。

sentences.en: And if you say, oh, it's not for me, I don't like peppered brandy.
sentences.zh: 如果你说，哦，这不适合我，我不喜欢加胡椒的白兰地。

sentences.en: I don't like trained bears either while we're at it.
sentences.zh: 说到这儿，我也不喜欢训练过的熊。

sentences.en: The bear has been trained not just to offer you cups of brandy, but to strip you naked.
sentences.zh: 这头熊受过训练，不仅会给你端白兰地，还会把你的衣服扒光。

sentences.en: Imagine being stripped by a bear.
sentences.zh: 想象一下被一头熊剥光衣服。

sentences.en: That's not the kind of thing that Wojtek got up to.
sentences.zh: 沃伊泰克可没干过这种事。

sentences.en: I'm glad to say.
sentences.zh: 我很庆幸。

sentences.en: No, no, our previous bear.
sentences.zh: 不，不，这是我们以前那头熊。

sentences.en: We don't know the name of this bear, but it sounds absolutely splendid.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这头熊的名字，但它听起来绝对棒极了。

sentences.en: So as time goes on, this becomes more and more formalized and ritualized.
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，这一切变得越来越形式化、仪式化。

sentences.en: So by the 1690s, the Jolly Company has been organized into what Peter calls the all joking, all drunken synod of fools and jesters.
sentences.zh: 因此到了17世纪90年代，欢乐连被组织成了彼得所说的全员恶搞、全员醉酒的傻子与小丑主教会议。

sentences.en: This clearly does have a slight political edge because it's a parody of the of the church.
sentences.zh: 这显然带有轻微的政治色彩，因为它是对教会的一种模仿。

sentences.en: So they have cardinals, they have bishops, they have deacons.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有红衣主教，有主教，有执事。

sentences.en: Peter is just a deacon.
sentences.zh: 彼得只是个执事。

sentences.en: But Dominic, the fact that there are cardinals, which you don't get in the Orthodox Church, but you do get in the Catholic Church.
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，东正教里是没有红衣主教的，但天主教里有，既然存在红衣主教这一事实……

sentences.en: I mean, he can say this is a parody of the heretical Caesarist Catholic Church, can't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他可以说是对异端凯撒主义天主教教会的模仿，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, he can.
sentences.zh: 对，他可以这么说。

sentences.en: I think what lies behind this.
sentences.zh: 我想这背后的动机是。

sentences.en: So actually, he started doing this, the all drunken synod, after there was the accession of a new patriarch who was very anti-Western, very traditionaliSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他开始举办这个全员醉酒的主教会议，是在一位非常反西方、非常传统的年轻大主教上任之后。

sentences.en: He was called Adrian.
sentences.zh: 他叫阿德里安。

sentences.en: And Peter despised Adrian.
sentences.zh: 彼得极其鄙视阿德里安。

sentences.en: And I think he clearly wanted the all drunken synod to mock the Orthodox Church, but he knew he couldn't do it directly.
sentences.zh: 我想他显然是想通过全员醉酒的主教会议来嘲讽东正教，但他知道自己不能直接这么做。

sentences.en: So the rituals are Catholic, exactly as you say, because it would be far too subversive.
sentences.zh: 所以这些仪式都是天主教的，正如你所说，因为直接做的话就太具颠覆性了。

sentences.en: Just on Peter's attitude to the Orthodox Church.
sentences.zh: 仅就彼得对东正教的态度而言。

sentences.en: I mean, he is still a devout believer, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他仍然是一个虔诚的信徒，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, he is.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是。

sentences.en: It's not like he is a kind of Frederick the Great or someone like that who is contemptuous of Christianity.
sentences.zh: 他可不像腓特烈大帝或诸如此类蔑视基督教的人。

sentences.en: No, he's not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，他一点也不蔑视。

sentences.en: He is still pious, but he's fascinated by other forms of Christianity, as we'll see.
sentences.zh: 他依然很虔诚，但正如我们所见，他对其他形式的基督教充满了迷恋。

sentences.en: When he goes abroad, he wants to find out all about them.
sentences.zh: 当他出国时，他想把这一切了解透彻。

sentences.en: He's curious.
sentences.zh: 他很好奇。

sentences.en: Yeah, so that's why he's talking to Gilbert Burnett.
sentences.zh: 对，所以这就是为什么他要跟吉尔伯特·伯内特交谈。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say he's a very violent man.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以说他是一个非常暴力的人。

sentences.en: He's very impatient, but he's not intolerant of other ideas.
sentences.zh: 他非常急躁，但他对其他观点并不偏狭。

sentences.en: He's interested in other ideas, I think, which makes him different from a lot of Russian Tsars.
sentences.zh: 我对他的看法是，他对其他观点很感兴趣，这使他与许多俄国沙皇有所不同。

sentences.en: But you still wouldn't want to see him coming towards you with a pair of bellows.
sentences.zh: 但你大概还是不想看到他拿着个风箱朝你走来。

sentences.en: A pair of bellows and a bear.
sentences.zh: 一个风箱和一头熊。

sentences.en: That's terrifying.
sentences.zh: 那太吓人了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he has a mock Prince Pope, who's his old tutor, who's a man called Nikita Zotov, who presides over this synod.
sentences.zh: 所以他有一个仿冒的教皇，也就是他的老导师，一个叫尼基塔·佐托夫的男子，由他来主持这个会议。

sentences.en: So on feast days, on religious feast days, to mock the church, they have their biggest kind of antics and rituals.
sentences.zh: 因此在节日里，在宗教节日里，为了嘲讽教会，他们会进行最大规模的滑稽表演和仪式。

sentences.en: And the Pope wears gloves made of mice skins.
sentences.zh: 教皇戴着老鼠皮做的手套。

sentences.en: It's bonkers.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So on Christmas, they ride around on sleighs.
sentences.zh: 所以在圣诞节，他们会坐着雪橇到处转悠。

sentences.en: A sleigh drawn by 12 bald men.
sentences.zh: 由12个光头男子拉着的雪橇。

sentences.en: The mock Pope is wearing a tin hat and a costume made of playing cards.
sentences.zh: 那个假教皇戴着锡帽，穿着扑克牌做成的服装。

sentences.en: Guards.
sentences.zh: 卫兵。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Which seems bonkers.
sentences.zh: 这听起来太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And the others are all wearing their clothes inside out, as you said.
sentences.zh: 其他人也都像你说的把衣服穿反了。

sentences.en: Gloves of mice skins.
sentences.zh: 老鼠皮手套。

sentences.en: Oh, I thought it was the Pope who wore them.
sentences.zh: 哦，我还以为是教皇戴呢。

sentences.en: So everyone's wearing it.
sentences.zh: 原来每个人都戴着。

sentences.en: That's a lot of mice who've had to be killed.
sentences.zh: 那得杀多少只老鼠啊。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对啊。

sentences.en: And their sleighs are pulled by pigs and bears.
sentences.zh: 他们的雪橇是由猪和熊来拉的。

sentences.en: Such a lot of bears.
sentences.zh: 有这么多的熊。

sentences.en: I don't believe you could train a bear to pull it.
sentences.zh: 我不相信你能训练一头熊去拉雪橇。

sentences.en: Well, maybe you could.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许你可以吧。

sentences.en: Surely not the same bear who's stripping people naked.
sentences.zh: 肯定不是那头把人扒光的熊吧？

sentences.en: Well, I think you can train a bear to strip you bare if you don't want a mug of spiced whiskey or whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想如果你不想要一杯香料威士忌或别的什么东西的话，你确实可以训练一头熊来把你扒光。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: Anyway, so is Peter doing anything other than sort of blowing people up with bellows and things?
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，所以彼得除了用风箱炸人之类的事，还在干别的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's doing loads of naval stuff.
sentences.zh: 他在搞大量海军方面的事。

sentences.en: So he goes up to Archangel.
sentences.zh: 所以他去了阿尔汉格尔斯克。

sentences.en: You mentioned Archangel in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 你在上一集里提到过阿尔汉格尔斯克。

sentences.en: It's on the White Sea.
sentences.zh: 它位于白海。

sentences.en: It's the only Russian outlet to the sea.
sentences.zh: 这是俄国唯一通往海洋的出口。

sentences.en: It's a little bit of a forerunner of St. Petersburg, actually, because it has English and Dutch sailors who live there.
sentences.zh: 其实它有点像是圣彼得堡的先驱，因为那里住着英国和荷兰的水手。

sentences.en: It has sort of churches, Protestant churches.
sentences.zh: 那里有某种教堂，新教教堂。

sentences.en: When you go to Archangel, there's taverns full of Dutch sea captains smoking pipes and talking about William of Orange.
sentences.zh: 当你去阿尔汉格尔斯克时，酒馆里到处都是抽着烟斗、谈论奥兰治的威廉的荷兰船长。

sentences.en: And he loves that.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And he goes up there.
sentences.zh: 于是他北上了。

sentences.en: And it's actually at this point that he designs a flag for his sort of navy.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，他为他的海军设计了一面旗帜。

sentences.en: Because he's very interested in Holland, he models it on the flag of the Dutch States General, but he reorders the colours.
sentences.zh: 因为他对荷兰非常感兴趣，他以荷兰国会旗帜为蓝本，但重新排列了颜色。

sentences.en: So it's the white, blue and red flag of today's Russian Federation.
sentences.zh: 所以它就是今天俄罗斯联邦的白、蓝、红三色旗。

sentences.en: So it's basically Dutch.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上是荷兰式的。

sentences.en: It's Dutch, exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全是荷兰式的。

sentences.en: So the Russian navy is English and the flag is Dutch.
sentences.zh: 所以俄罗斯海军是英国式的，旗帜是荷兰式的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Putin keeps quiet about that, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 普京对这一点避而不谈，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, he doesn't play that up as much as he could.
sentences.zh: 对，他没有像原本可以的那样大肆宣扬这一点。

sentences.en: So his first war is he thinks I'll have a little crack at the Ottomans because they'd still got this deal with the Polish, Lithuanian Commonwealth and co.
sentences.zh: 所以他的第一场战争是，他心想我要去挑衅一下奥斯曼人，因为他们当时和波兰立陶宛联邦等人还有个协议。

sentences.en: They're meant to be fighting the Ottomans.
sentences.zh: 他们本该和奥斯曼人作战。

sentences.en: So he decides he wants to capture Azov on the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定攻占黑海边的亚速。

sentences.en: The first go at it in 1695 doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 1695年的第一次尝试没有成功。

sentences.en: But in 1696, he goes down the River Don with loads of Cossacks and he captures Azov from the Ottomans.
sentences.zh: 但在1696年，他带着大批哥萨克顺着顿河南下，从奥斯曼人手中夺取了亚速。

sentences.en: And this is the first Russian victory for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 这是俄罗斯20年来取得的第一场胜利。

sentences.en: So it's a great moment.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个伟大的时刻。

sentences.en: And he has his outlet now.
sentences.zh: 他现在有了出海口。

sentences.en: It's not quite on the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 虽然还算不上真正的黑海。

sentences.en: It's only on the Sea of Azov.
sentences.zh: 它只是亚速海。

sentences.en: So he needs to go a little bit further to get into the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 所以他需要再往前走一点才能进入黑海。

sentences.en: However, it's a start.
sentences.zh: 不过，这是一个开始。

sentences.en: He has a triumph in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他在莫斯科举行了凯旋游行。

sentences.en: And here again, you see his kind of westernizing ambitions.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你再次看到了他那西化雄心。

sentences.en: Because previously, when Russian Tsars had triumphs, they were very orthodox occasions.
sentences.zh: 因为在此之前，俄国沙皇凯旋时，都是非常传统的东正教活动。

sentences.en: There's lots of sort of chanting and waving around of icons.
sentences.zh: 有大量的吟唱和圣像挥舞。

sentences.en: So very second Rome.
sentences.zh: 非常具有第二罗马的风格。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: But Peter's is really very first Rome.
sentences.zh: 但彼得的游行非常有第一罗马的风格。

sentences.en: He has statues of Hercules and of Mars.
sentences.zh: 他有大力神和战神的雕像。

sentences.en: They put Julius Caesar's, I came, I saw, I conquered, Veni, Vidi, Viki on kind of classical gates.
sentences.zh: 他们在古典风格的城门上贴出了尤利乌斯·凯撒的“我来、我见、我征服”（Veni, Vidi, Vici）。

sentences.en: And as always, Peter, his role-playing, his performative humility is on display.
sentences.zh: 而且一如既往地，彼得展现了他那种角色扮演式的、表演性的谦逊。

sentences.en: So he gets this bloke who was the Prince Pope, who presumably is not now dressed in playing cards with kind of my skin gloves, to lead the procession.
sentences.zh: 于是他让那个曾担任教皇的家伙——现在大概没穿扑克牌服装也没戴鼠皮手套了——来带领游行队伍。

sentences.en: And he walks with the captains of his galleys, wearing an ordinary German captain's uniform.
sentences.zh: 他自己则和划桨船的船长们一起步行，穿着普通的德国船长制服。

sentences.en: And he'd performed very bravely, hadn't he, in the campaign against Azov, as an artillery man?
sentences.zh: 而且他在亚速战役中作为炮手表现得非常勇敢，对吧？

sentences.en: He had.
sentences.zh: 他的确很勇敢。

sentences.en: He'd done well.
sentences.zh: 他干得很好。

sentences.en: He'd done very well.
sentences.zh: 他干得非常出色。

sentences.en: And then just weeks after this victory comes an unbelievable announcement from the foreign ministry.
sentences.zh: 就在这场胜利后仅仅几周，外交部发布了一个令人难以置信的公告。

sentences.en: Peter is sending a great embassy to Europe, to England, to Denmark, to the Dutch states, to Brandenburg, to Venice.
sentences.zh: 彼得要派遣一个宏大的使团前往欧洲，去往英国、丹麦、荷兰各省、勃兰登堡和威尼斯。

sentences.en: This embassy is going to be led by his mate, the France Lefort, and they're going to recruit officers and shipwrights and sailors to come back to Russia and to build a fleet.
sentences.zh: 这个使团将由他的好友弗朗兹·勒福尔率领，他们要去招募军官、造船工和水手回到俄国建造舰队。

sentences.en: And they're going to learn from the advanced nations of the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他们将向西方的先进国家学习。

sentences.en: Now, this is an extraordinary thing for a Tsar to do, to send some of his closest mates.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于一个沙皇来说，派他最亲密的几个朋友出国，这是一件非同寻常的事。

sentences.en: But then a rumour goes around Moscow, Peter's actually going to go with them.
sentences.zh: 但随后莫斯科流传起一个传言，彼得竟然要亲自随行。

sentences.en: And he's not going to go with them as the Tsar.
sentences.zh: 而且他不是以沙皇的身份随行。

sentences.en: He's going to go as a member of the diplomatic staff in disguise.
sentences.zh: 他要乔装打扮成外交随员随行。

sentences.en: So this is his business about pretending he's not the Tsar, which he loves to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是他那种假装自己不是沙皇的把戏，他最喜欢这么干了。

sentences.en: Even though he's by miles the tallest member of the embassy.
sentences.zh: 尽管他是使团里个子最高的人，高出了一大截。

sentences.en: He's the tallest person.
sentences.zh: 他是最高的人。

sentences.en: So there are multiple reasons why he wants to do this, because this is an extraordinary thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他想这么做有多种原因，因为这是一件极其罕见的事。

sentences.en: No Russian Tsar has ever travelled outside Russia, except when they're fighting, before.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，除了打仗，没有任何一个俄国沙皇离开过俄国领土。

sentences.en: It's unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 这是史无前例的。

sentences.en: Now, one reason is he wants to get allies to strengthen the alliance against the Ottomans, because he's very keen on this Black Sea kind of breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 现在，其中一个原因是想拉拢盟友以加强反奥斯曼帝国的同盟，因为他非常热衷于在黑海方向取得这种突破。

sentences.en: But the more obvious kind of personal reason is that he is just absolutely fascinated with the West, with Holland and England in particular.
sentences.zh: 但更明显、更个人的原因是，他简直对西方、特别是荷兰和英国着迷至极。

sentences.en: He wants to go to their dockyards.
sentences.zh: 他想去他们的造船厂。

sentences.en: He wants to study their ship building techniques.
sentences.zh: 他想研究他们的造船技术。

sentences.en: And he clearly knows, I think, as so many Russians know, that the gap between Russia and the West has never been greater.
sentences.zh: 而且他心里很清楚，就像许多俄国人所意识到的那样，俄国与西方的差距从未像现在这样巨大。

sentences.en: That in the West, this is the age of Newton, of Leibniz, of the financial and scientific revolutions, of stock exchanges and newspapers and things.
sentences.zh: 在西方，这是牛顿、莱布尼茨的时代，是金融和科学革命的时代，是证券交易所和报纸等事物的时代。

sentences.en: And Russia is in danger of falling centuries behind.
sentences.zh: 而俄国正面临着落后几个世纪的危险。

sentences.en: And he has a seal made that has the inscription, I am a student and I am looking for teachers.
sentences.zh: 他甚至让人刻了一枚印章，上面刻着：“我是个学生，我在寻找老师。”

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, so he's pretty explicit about it.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，他对此毫不掩饰。

sentences.en: Why would the Dutch or the English or whoever be willing to teach a potential rival about the reasons for their lead?
sentences.zh: 为什么荷兰人、英国人或其他什么人会愿意把他们领先的原因教给一个潜在的竞争对手呢？

sentences.en: I mean, if you have a technological lead, why would you share it with somebody who is potentially quite a major threat?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你在技术上处于领先地位，你为什么会与一个可能构成重大威胁的人分享呢？

sentences.en: A fairly obvious reason, I would have thought, is that he's Orthodox and he's not Catholic.
sentences.zh: 我想一个相当显而易见的原因是，他是东正教徒而不是天主教徒。

sentences.en: So if you're a Protestant power, he could conceivably be an ally against Louis XIV, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一个新教强权，他完全有可能成为对抗路易十四的盟友，对吧？

sentences.en: Who is the great figure of the age, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 路易十四可是那个时代风头最劲的人物，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He doesn't go to France in this trip.
sentences.zh: 他这次旅行没有去法国。

sentences.en: He goes to the two great Protestant adversaries of France.
sentences.zh: 他去了法国的两个伟大新教对头那里。

sentences.en: I think they're flattered, England and the Dutch Republic, by Peter's attentions.
sentences.zh: 我想英国和荷兰共和国对彼得的重视感到受宠若惊。

sentences.en: And maybe they're hoping to, well, Gilbert Burnett.
sentences.zh: 也许他们也希望……嗯，吉尔伯特·伯内特。

sentences.en: I mean, he's clearly trying to win Peter for Anglicanism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他显然在试图争取彼得皈依英国国教。

sentences.en: For Anglicanism, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所见，是为了争取英国国教。

sentences.en: As we will see, people in England thought, this is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所见，英国人当时觉得，这太棒了。

sentences.en: We could basically get an ally in Russia.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上能在俄罗斯获得一个盟友。

sentences.en: We could have an Anglican ally.
sentences.zh: 我们可以有一个信奉英国国教的盟友。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I know that sounds bonkers.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很疯狂。

sentences.en: But is it any more bonkers than the Tsar of Russia going in disguise on a massive gap year to the West?
sentences.zh: 不过，这比起俄罗斯沙皇微服私访、在西方度过漫长间隔年还要疯狂吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it is.
sentences.zh: 我觉得并不比这更疯狂。

sentences.en: I suppose not.
sentences.zh: 我也觉得不会。

sentences.en: So he decides he's going to set off.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定启程。

sentences.en: His mother, by the way, is dead at this point.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，此时他的母亲已经去世了。

sentences.en: And actually, his brother, Ivan, has died as well.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的兄弟伊凡也已经去世了。

sentences.en: So he leaves his mate, Romadanovsky, the guy who has the bear.
sentences.zh: 因此他把好友罗马达诺夫斯基——那个养熊的家伙——留了下来。

sentences.en: So the Prince Caesar.
sentences.zh: 也就是凯撒亲王。

sentences.en: The Prince Caesar, as he's called.
sentences.zh: 正如人们所称的那样，凯撒亲王。

sentences.en: He says, you're commanding the troops.
sentences.zh: 他对对方说，你来统帅军队。

sentences.en: You have basically command of law and order while I'm gone.
sentences.zh: 我不在的时候，治安和法律基本上就由你全权负责。

sentences.en: As he leaves, he has a farewell banquet and he hears that there's been some bitching among the Streltsy about him.
sentences.zh: 他临走前举办了一场告别宴会，席间听说斯特列利齐近卫军中有人在背后对他说三道四。

sentences.en: They've been saying, oh, he's going off to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在说，哦，他这是要去西方了。

sentences.en: You know, he's going to betray us all to foreigners.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他这是要把我们全都出卖给外国人。

sentences.en: And he has this Streltsy colonel and two noblemen executed.
sentences.zh: 于是他下令处决了一名斯特列利齐上校和两名贵族。

sentences.en: He has their limbs cut off with an axe and then they're beheaded.
sentences.zh: 他让人用斧头砍断他们的四肢，然后再将他们斩首。

sentences.en: And then he gets the coffin of Sophia's uncle.
sentences.zh: 接着，他弄来了索菲亚叔叔的棺材。

sentences.en: So one of the Milislavsky family.
sentences.zh: 也就是米洛斯拉夫斯基家族的成员之一。

sentences.en: He gets this coffin dragged by pigs into Red Square.
sentences.zh: 他让人用猪把这口棺材拖到红场。

sentences.en: What is it with pigs?
sentences.zh: 这猪是怎么回事？

sentences.en: There's obviously a whole kind of stables full of pigs who are trained to drag things.
sentences.zh: 显然，那里有一个马厩，里面养满了受过训练、专门用来拖东西的猪。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the coffin is opened beneath the chopping block where these guys have been executed so that their blood will spatter the face of Sophia's dead uncle.
sentences.zh: 棺材被打开放在行刑的斩首台下方，这样他们的血就会溅到索菲亚死去的叔叔的脸上。

sentences.en: I mean, this is by no means the most sadistic thing that Peter will do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝不是彼得做过的最虐待狂的事情。

sentences.en: He loves a really, really horrendous kind of sadistic jape.
sentences.zh: 他非常喜欢极其可怕、近乎虐待狂的恶作剧。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of them to come.
sentences.zh: 而且以后还会有很多这样的恶作剧。

sentences.en: So after he's done this, he sets off.
sentences.zh: 做完这些后，他便动身了。

sentences.en: He's traveling as Peter Mikhailov.
sentences.zh: 他化名为彼得·米哈伊洛夫四处旅行。

sentences.en: There's 250 people, loads of noblemen, musicians, coachmen, priests, secretaries, four dwarfs.
sentences.zh: 随行人员有250人，包括大批贵族、音乐家、车夫、牧师、秘书以及四个侏儒。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: He's Peter Mikhailov.
sentences.zh: 他就是彼得·米哈伊洛夫。

sentences.en: If you tell anybody who he is, he will kill you.
sentences.zh: 如果你向任何人透露他的真实身份，他就会杀了你。

sentences.en: But he wants people to kind of recognize him and be polite to him at the same time.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他又希望别人能认出他来并对他保持礼貌。

sentences.en: So he's using the incognito thing basically as a way to get out of formalities.
sentences.zh: 所以他使用匿名身份，基本上只是为了摆脱繁文缛节。

sentences.en: Yeah, all the boring stuff.
sentences.zh: 对，就是所有那些无聊的规矩。

sentences.en: But he still wants to see fireworks displays in his honor and for people to present him with enormous goblets of wine.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然希望看到为他举办的烟花汇演，希望有人向他敬献巨大的酒杯。

sentences.en: He's a cakeiSt.
sentences.zh: 他真是个两面讨好的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's a total cakeiSt.
sentences.zh: 对，他绝对是个两面讨巧的家伙。

sentences.en: He wants to have his cake and eat it.
sentences.zh: 他既想占有蛋糕，又想把它吃掉。

sentences.en: So they set off.
sentences.zh: 于是他们出发了。

sentences.en: They cross the frontier into what's then called Livonia, which is kind of Estonia, Latvia, which is part of the Swedish Empire.
sentences.zh: 他们穿过边界，进入当时被称为利沃尼亚的地区，也就是现在的爱沙尼亚和拉脱维亚一部分，当时属于瑞典帝国。

sentences.en: And they arrive in Riga.
sentences.zh: 他们抵达了里加。

sentences.en: Peter does not like Riga at all.
sentences.zh: 彼得一点也不喜欢里加。

sentences.en: And he hates the Swedes because the Swedes take the incognito thing very seriously.
sentences.zh: 而且他讨厌瑞典人，因为瑞典人把匿名这件事看得非常严肃。

sentences.en: And they say they don't have a banquet for him.
sentences.zh: 他们说不会为他举办宴会。

sentences.en: You know, the Swedes respond exactly as you would expect the Swedes to.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，瑞典人的反应和你预想的一模一样。

sentences.en: Very sober.
sentences.zh: 非常冷静。

sentences.en: Very sober.
sentences.zh: 非常严肃。

sentences.en: They say, well, if you're not Peter the Great, great.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，如果你不是彼得大帝，那就太好了。

sentences.en: No fireworks.
sentences.zh: 没有烟花。

sentences.en: By the way, you have to pay for your own board and lodging.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，你的伙食费和住宿费得自己出。

sentences.en: This he's really offended by, the Swedish lack of hospitality.
sentences.zh: 瑞典人这种缺乏待客之道的做法让他感到非常被冒犯。

sentences.en: He's shocked at this.
sentences.zh: 对此他感到震惊。

sentences.en: But also, he's fascinated by kind of fortifications and things.
sentences.zh: 不过同时，他又对各种防御工事之类的事情充满着迷。

sentences.en: So he goes off to inspect the defences of Riga.
sentences.zh: 于是他跑去视察里加的防御设施。

sentences.en: But because he's incognito, a Swedish sentry spots him and threatens to shoot him.
sentences.zh: 但由于他隐瞒了身份，一名瑞典哨兵认出了他并威胁要开枪打他。

sentences.en: Yeah, but also, Dominic, I mean, even if they did, this is a fortress next to a potential enemy.
sentences.zh: 对，但是多米尼克，我的意思是，即便他们真这么做了，这也是一座紧邻潜在敌人的堡垒啊。

sentences.en: And then the leader of that enemy is sketching your fortress.
sentences.zh: 然后这个敌人的首领竟然在画你们的堡垒。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, the Russians, they don't tend to like, you know, foreigners turning up and making sketches of their nuclear refineries.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，俄罗斯人通常也不喜欢外国人跑来画他们核设施的草图。

sentences.en: No, right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: If Vladimir Putin turned up at a British submarine base in disguise, clearly, obviously Vladimir Putin, and then was offended when people challenged him.
sentences.zh: 如果弗拉基米尔·普京乔装打扮出现在英国的潜艇基地，很明显所有人都能看出他就是普京，然后当人们盘问他时他还觉得被冒犯了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But he hated this.
sentences.zh: 但他对此恨之入骨。

sentences.en: He hated Riga.
sentences.zh: 他恨里加。

sentences.en: And 13 years later, when his army was attacking Riga, he insisted on firing the first shells into the city.
sentences.zh: 13年后，当他的军队进攻里加时，他坚持要亲手向这座城市发射第一轮炮弹。

sentences.en: I do like a man who bears a grudge.
sentences.zh: 我还真挺欣赏这种记仇的人。

sentences.en: He said, I thank God for allowing me to see the beginning of our revenge on this accursed place.
sentences.zh: 他说，我感谢上帝让我看到我们开始对这个该死的地方进行复仇。

sentences.en: I mean, you really wouldn't want him as an enemy, would you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你真的不会想与他为敌，对吧？

sentences.en: You wouldn't want him as a friend either, frankly, if he comes at you with some bellows.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，如果他拿着风箱朝你走来，你也不会想跟他做朋友。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He goes into a place called Courland, which is now kind of Lithuania.
sentences.zh: 他来到了一个叫库尔兰的地方，也就是现在的立陶宛一部分。

sentences.en: He goes to Königsberg, now Kaliningrad.
sentences.zh: 他去了哥尼斯堡，也就是现在的加里宁格勒。

sentences.en: He meets the elector of Brandenburg, who is the future Frederick I of Prussia.
sentences.zh: 他见到了勃兰登堡选帝侯，也就是未来的普鲁士国王腓特烈一世。

sentences.en: They have a great time.
sentences.zh: 他们玩得很开心。

sentences.en: They go hunting.
sentences.zh: 他们去打猎。

sentences.en: They have the fireworks display.
sentences.zh: 他们观看了烟花汇演。

sentences.en: They watch bears fighting, this stage a bear fight.
sentences.zh: 他们观看狗熊打架，这里上演了一场熊类搏斗。

sentences.en: Do you know, I mean, I had no idea that bear action played such a part in royal embassies and entertainment in the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我压根不知道熊斗在18世纪的皇家使团和娱乐活动中占有这么重要的地位。

sentences.en: When we get on to Augustus the Strong, all kinds of activities with animals there.
sentences.zh: 等我们聊到强者奥古斯都时，那里还有各种各样的动物活动呢。

sentences.en: Well, foxes.
sentences.zh: 哦，还有狐狸。

sentences.en: So he meets Sophia of Hanover, who is the mother of George I.
sentences.zh: 于是他见到了汉诺威的索菲亚，也就是乔治一世的母亲。

sentences.en: So she's going to be Queen Anne's heir to maintain the Protestant succession.
sentences.zh: 所以她将成为安妮女王的继承人，以维护新教王位的继承。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is a very funny scene because he'd never met aristocratic Western women before.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常搞笑的场景，因为他以前从未见过西方的贵族女性。

sentences.en: And he's shown in to see them.
sentences.zh: 他被带进去拜访她们。

sentences.en: He's very embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 他感到非常尴尬。

sentences.en: He doesn't know what to say.
sentences.zh: 他不知道该说些什么。

sentences.en: He literally covered his face with his hands in embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 他尴尬得 literalmente（字面意思）用双手捂住了脸。

sentences.en: And he sort of muttered from behind his hands, I don't know what to say.
sentences.zh: 他在双手后面嘟囔着说，我不知道该说什么。

sentences.en: And Sophia and her daughter are very nice to him.
sentences.zh: 索菲亚和她的女儿对他都非常好。

sentences.en: They say, oh, come on, it's fine.
sentences.zh: 她们说，哎呀，别这样，没事的。

sentences.en: They have some music.
sentences.zh: 她们放了一些音乐。

sentences.en: They bring in some Hanoverian children, including the future George II.
sentences.zh: 她们带进来一些汉诺威的孩子，其中包括未来的乔治二世。

sentences.en: And he loves George II.
sentences.zh: 他非常喜欢乔治二世。

sentences.en: He hugs him and kisses him and sort of puts him on his lap and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他又抱又亲这个孩子，还把他抱在自己膝盖上之类的。

sentences.en: I mean, George II is 14.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，乔治二世当时已经14岁了。

sentences.en: He probably doesn't want to be kissed and hugged by a massive great Blake with a hairy moustache.
sentences.zh: 他可能并不想被一个留着浓密胡须的大块头又亲又抱。

sentences.en: And also he dances, doesn't he, with German women and is startled to discover that they're wearing these strange contraptions called corsets.
sentences.zh: 而且他还跟德国女性跳舞，并且惊讶地发现她们穿着一种叫作紧身胸衣的奇怪玩意儿。

sentences.en: Because no Russian woman wears a corset.
sentences.zh: 因为没有任何俄罗斯女性会穿紧身胸衣。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he's very taken with that.
sentences.zh: 所以他对这一点非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: He cries out, these German women have devilish hard bones.
sentences.zh: 他大声喊道，这些德国女人有着魔鬼般坚硬的骨头。

sentences.en: And there's all much laughing.
sentences.zh: 现场爆发出一阵大笑。

sentences.en: There's a lot of laughing.
sentences.zh: 笑声不断。

sentences.en: And actually, they are quite fond of him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她们还挺喜欢他的。

sentences.en: They were worried that he would get very drunk.
sentences.zh: 她们原本担心他会喝得酩酊大醉。

sentences.en: And he always restrains himself in the presence of aristocratic women.
sentences.zh: 但在贵族女性面前，他总是克制自己。

sentences.en: But then the people that he's traveling with, so all his mates and hangers on, all the lads.
sentences.zh: 不过随行的那些人，也就是他所有的死党和随从、那些小伙子们。

sentences.en: Jolly company.
sentences.zh: 真是一群快活的伴侣。

sentences.en: They get massively drunk.
sentences.zh: 他们全都喝得烂醉如泥。

sentences.en: And they make up for it.
sentences.zh: 他们把这一点给补回来了。

sentences.en: And this is definitely a theme of the trip.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是此次旅行的一个主题。

sentences.en: So eventually, he gets to Holland.
sentences.zh: 最终，他到达了荷兰。

sentences.en: And he is so excited about this.
sentences.zh: 他对此兴奋不已。

sentences.en: It's actually quite sweet.
sentences.zh: 其实这还挺可爱的。

sentences.en: He goes on ahead of the rest of his party because he just can't wait.
sentences.zh: 他比随行大部队先行一步，因为他实在等不及了。

sentences.en: And his destination is a place called Zandam, which is a great kind of shipyard.
sentences.zh: 他的目的地是一个叫赞丹的地方，那是一个非常了不起的造船基地。

sentences.en: And they claim in this place that they're the best shipyard in Holland.
sentences.zh: 当地人声称自己是荷兰最好的造船厂。

sentences.en: There are 50 different companies and they make more than 300 ships a year.
sentences.zh: 那里有50家不同的公司，每年建造300多艘船。

sentences.en: So this is like, for Peter, this is Disneyland.
sentences.zh: 所以对彼得来说，这就好比是迪士尼乐园。

sentences.en: Ship heaven.
sentences.zh: 造船的天堂。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: So he arrives on a Sunday.
sentences.zh: 于是他在一个星期天抵达。

sentences.en: And immediately, he bumps into a bloke who'd once worked for him in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 刚一到，他就撞见了一个曾经在莫斯科为他工作过的家伙。

sentences.en: A blacksmith called Gerrit KiSt.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫格里特·基斯特的铁匠。

sentences.en: And Peter hugs him, kisses him and stuff.
sentences.zh: 彼得又是拥抱又是亲吻他。

sentences.en: And Kist says, come and stay in the house next door.
sentences.zh: 基斯特说，来隔壁的房子住吧。

sentences.en: I mean, Kist just can't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，基斯特简直不敢相信这一切。

sentences.en: It's just mind-boggling to him that the Tsar of Russia has turned up in his town.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯沙皇竟然来到了他的小镇，这让他感到匪夷所思。

sentences.en: And says, I'll move in next door to you, which is what happens.
sentences.zh: 并且说要搬到你隔壁住，结果真的就这么发生了。

sentences.en: And the next day is a Monday morning.
sentences.zh: 第二天是星期一早晨。

sentences.en: Peter gets up.
sentences.zh: 彼得起了床。

sentences.en: He's obviously got some money.
sentences.zh: 他显然带了一些钱。

sentences.en: He goes off and he buys a load of tools.
sentences.zh: 他出门去买了一大堆工具。

sentences.en: And then he goes to a shipyard run by a man called Linst Rogger.
sentences.zh: 然后他去了一家由一个叫林斯特·罗格的人经营的造船厂。

sentences.en: And he signs up to work in the shipyard under the name Peter Mikhailov.
sentences.zh: 他以彼得·米哈伊洛夫的名字报名在造船厂工作。

sentences.en: I mean, can you imagine Donald Trump doing this?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你能想象唐纳德·特朗普做这种事吗？

sentences.en: You know, signing up to work in a call center?
sentences.zh: 比如说，报名去呼叫中心工作？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不可能。

sentences.en: He wants to send them to Moscow as well.
sentences.zh: 他也想把这些寄到莫斯科。

sentences.en: So that's testimony to the fact that the English are becoming a polite and commercial people, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这证明了英国人正在变得彬彬有礼、富有商业头脑，对吧？

sentences.en: That they have shops where you can buy a stuffed crocodile.
sentences.zh: 他们竟然有能买到标本鳄鱼的商店。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Our taxidermist is second to none, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以公正地说，我们的动物标本剥制师堪称一流。

sentences.en: He becomes friends with a bloke called the Marquess of Carmarthen.
sentences.zh: 他和一个叫卡马森侯爵的家伙成为了朋友。

sentences.en: And he goes to the pub with this bloke so often that the pub is renamed the Tsar of Russia.
sentences.zh: 他和这家伙去酒吧的频率如此之高，以至于该酒吧都被更名为“俄罗斯沙皇”了。

sentences.en: And Carmarthen says, oh, I know who you'd like to meet.
sentences.zh: 卡马森说，哦，我知道你想见谁。

sentences.en: And he introduces him to an actress called Letitia Cross, who becomes his mistress while he's in England and moves in with him in the student house.
sentences.zh: 于是他把他介绍给了一位名叫莱蒂蒂亚·克罗斯的女演员，她在彼得留在英国期间成了他的情妇，并搬进学生宿舍和他一起生活。

sentences.en: And what language do they speak?
sentences.zh: 他们说的是什么语言？

sentences.en: Is it the language of love?
sentences.zh: 是爱情的语言吗？

sentences.en: The language of love, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这就是爱情的语言。

sentences.en: They speak the language of love, right?
sentences.zh: 他们说的是爱情的语言，对吧？

sentences.en: Anyway, he's off the Strand.
sentences.zh: 总之，他住在河岸街附近。

sentences.en: So he's very central and there's more trouble with crowds.
sentences.zh: 所以位置非常中心，但人群也带来了更多麻烦。

sentences.en: And so William III's government say, look, we'll find you a house across the river.
sentences.zh: 因此，威廉三世的政府说，听着，我们会在河对岸给你找栋房子。

sentences.en: And this is where we come to a single favourite episode in all of history.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们迎来整个历史上最喜欢的一个片段的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the essayist and kind of diarist and whatnot, John Evelyn has this house in Deptford.
sentences.zh: 因此，散文家、日记作家兼斜杠青年约翰·伊夫林在德普福德拥有这样一栋房子。

sentences.en: And Charles II had given John Evelyn a lease on this house.
sentences.zh: 查理二世曾将这栋房子的租约授予约翰·伊夫林。

sentences.en: And Evelyn had owned it for 45 years.
sentences.zh: 伊夫林已经拥有它45年了。

sentences.en: And he had set out what was regarded as arguably the greatest garden in England.
sentences.zh: 他打造了可以说是全英格兰最伟大的花园。

sentences.en: His pride and joy.
sentences.zh: 那是他的骄傲与欢乐。

sentences.en: It had a bowling green.
sentences.zh: 里面有草地保龄球场。

sentences.en: It had a terrace walk.
sentences.zh: 有露台散步道。

sentences.en: It had kitchen gardens.
sentences.zh: 有菜园。

sentences.en: It had a walled garden.
sentences.zh: 有带围墙的花园。

sentences.en: Now, when it was first mentioned to John Evelyn that Peter the Great might move in, he said, brilliant, because he's actually been renting it to a man called Admiral Benbow.
sentences.zh: 现在，当第一次有人向约翰·伊夫林提及彼得大帝可能会搬进来时，他说，太棒了，因为他之前其实是把房子租给了一个叫本博海军上将的人。

sentences.en: The pub in Treasure Island.
sentences.zh: 就是《金银岛》里的那个酒吧。

sentences.en: As in the pub.
sentences.zh: 就像那个酒吧一样。

sentences.en: Admiral Benbow had not been a good tenant.
sentences.zh: 本博海军上将并不是一个好租客。

sentences.en: There'd been a little bit of wear and tear and he hadn't looked after the garden properly.
sentences.zh: 房子有一些磨损，而且他也没有好好打理花园。

sentences.en: So John Evelyn said, oh, well, great.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰·伊夫林说，哦，好吧，太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, these Russians, they can't be any worse than Admiral Benbow.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些俄罗斯人总不可能比本博海军上将更糟吧。

sentences.en: And we will find out later in the episode exactly what went on.
sentences.zh: 我们将在本集后面揭晓到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: But it's very clear something has gone wrong when John Evelyn Stewart, after a few days, says, the house is full of people and right nasty.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，几天后，当约翰·伊夫林的管家说“房子里到处都是人，而且真他妈恶心”时，事情就已经出问题了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But how nasty, we will discover.
sentences.zh: 但究竟有多恶心，我们接下来会发现。

sentences.en: Anyway, while he's not smashing up the house, we mentioned Bishop Burnett from Wiltshire and the Salisbury area.
sentences.zh: 总之，当他没有在砸毁房子的时候，我们提到了来自威尔特郡和索尔兹伯里地区的伯内特主教。

sentences.en: Peter, he's been trying to convert Peter to Anglicanism.
sentences.zh: 彼得，他一直试图让彼得皈依英国国教。

sentences.en: But the people that Peter really loves meeting are very much friends of the show.
sentences.zh: 但彼得真正喜欢见的人其实是节目的老朋友。

sentences.en: Richard Nixon's favorite people, the Quakers.
sentences.zh: 理查德·尼克松最喜欢的人，贵格会教徒。

sentences.en: Always good to have a Quaker on the rest of his history.
sentences.zh: 在“其余的历史”里有个贵格会教徒总是不错的。

sentences.en: So Peter can't get enough of the Quakers.
sentences.zh: 所以彼得对贵格会教徒简直爱不释手。

sentences.en: He goes to prayer meetings.
sentences.zh: 他去参加祷告会。

sentences.en: They're quaking and doing what they do, being very sober and quaking.
sentences.zh: 他们浑身发抖，做着他们日常做的事，表现得非常严肃而且浑身发抖。

sentences.en: He says, this is absolutely amazing.
sentences.zh: 他说，这简直太惊人了。

sentences.en: I love this.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: He meets William Penn of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 他遇到了宾夕法尼亚的威廉·彭恩。

sentences.en: Well, presumably if they're quaking and Peter is given to convulsions, he'd feel quite at home, wouldn't he?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果他们浑身发抖，而彼得又容易抽搐的话，他大概会觉得宾至如归吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, he fits in.
sentences.zh: 对，他完美融入了。

sentences.en: For once, his twitching is not noticed.
sentences.zh: 难得的是，他的抽搐没有被注意到。

sentences.en: So William Penn of Pennsylvania fame, he is in between trips to Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 因此，大名鼎鼎的宾夕法尼亚人威廉·彭恩，正处于他几次前往宾夕法尼亚的间隙中。

sentences.en: He goes to the house at Deptford to talk to Peter.
sentences.zh: 他去了德普福德的房子与彼得交谈。

sentences.en: And they have a great chat in Dutch about Quakerism.
sentences.zh: 他们用荷兰语就贵格会教进行了愉快的交谈。

sentences.en: And afterwards, Peter says to his Russian friends, whoever could live according to such a doctrine would be truly happy.
sentences.zh: 事后，彼得对他的俄罗斯朋友们说，谁能按照这样的教义生活，谁就真的是幸福的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's amazing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太神奇了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because foreign visitors to London are impressed by the Quakers.
sentences.zh: 因为来到伦敦的外国游客对贵格会教徒印象深刻。

sentences.en: Because Voltaire, when he goes to London, will be similarly kind of wowed by them.
sentences.zh: 因为伏尔泰去伦敦时，也会同样被他们深深折服。

sentences.en: It's kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: It's clearly something about London that foreigners find interesting.
sentences.zh: 显然伦敦有某种东西让外国人觉得很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah, but not in a sort of freak show way, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，但不是那种看畸形秀的心态，对吧？

sentences.en: No, they're impressed by them.
sentences.zh: 不，他们对他们印象深刻。

sentences.en: They're impressed by it.
sentences.zh: 他们对这一点印象深刻。

sentences.en: He takes it really seriously.
sentences.zh: 他是真的很认真地对待这件事。

sentences.en: He does loads of fun tourist things.
sentences.zh: 他做了大量好玩的游客活动。

sentences.en: He basically follows the itinerary that you would follow if you came to London on a holiday now.
sentences.zh: 他基本上遵循了你现在如果去伦敦度假会走的行程。

sentences.en: He goes to Greenwich.
sentences.zh: 他去了格林威治。

sentences.en: He goes to the Tower of London.
sentences.zh: 他去了伦敦塔。

sentences.en: And they hide the axe with which Charles I had been decapitated, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们把查理一世被斩首的那把斧头藏起来了，对吧？

sentences.en: Because they're worried that if he finds it, he'll be so outraged he'll fling it in the Thames.
sentences.zh: 因为他们担心如果他发现了，会气愤填膺地把它扔进泰晤士河。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And my favourite tourist thing that he does, he goes to Parliament and he says, I'd love to see it.
sentences.zh: 而我最喜欢他做的游客活动是，他去议会说，我很想看看。

sentences.en: And he doesn't want to draw attention to himself.
sentences.zh: 他不想吸引人们对他的注意。

sentences.en: So he climbs up to the roof and he watches through a kind of upper gallery sort of skylight style window in the roof as William III is giving assent to tax bills in the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 所以他爬上了屋顶，通过屋顶上类似于高层走廊天窗风格的窗户，看着威廉三世在上议院批准税收法案。

sentences.en: And he says afterwards to his friends and whatnot, he says, well, we obviously couldn't do this in Russia because, you know, we have the absolute power of the Tsar in Russia.
sentences.zh: 事后他向朋友们感叹说，我们显然不能在俄罗斯这样做，因为你知道，我们在俄罗斯拥有沙皇的绝对权力。

sentences.en: We couldn't have any limitations.
sentences.zh: 我们不能有任何限制。

sentences.en: However, and I quote, it is good to hear subjects speaking truthfully and openly to their king.
sentences.zh: 然而，我引用原话，“听到臣民对他们的国王坦诚直言，这感觉真好。”

sentences.en: This is what we must learn from the English.
sentences.zh: 这是我们必须向英国人学习的。

sentences.en: Now, there's a lesson here for Vladimir Putin, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 现在，这对弗拉基米尔·普京来说是个教训，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, just on the topic of Vladimir Putin and London and Peter the Great.
sentences.zh: 好吧，就弗拉基米尔·普京、伦敦和彼得大帝这个话题而言。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: I don't know if you've seen, there's a statue of Peter the Great at Deptford.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有见过，德普福德有一尊彼得大帝的雕像。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Very weird.
sentences.zh: 非常怪异。

sentences.en: Done by this sculptor who also did one that was put up in the Peter and Paul fortress in St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 是由这位雕塑家完成的，他还创作了另一尊被竖立在圣彼得堡彼得保罗要塞里的雕像。

sentences.en: The sculptor is very keen on portraying Peter with very long, elongated fingers and limbs.
sentences.zh: 这位雕塑家非常热衷于将彼得描绘成有着非常修长的手指和四肢。

sentences.en: So he looks very peculiar.
sentences.zh: 所以他看起来非常奇特。

sentences.en: And a small head.
sentences.zh: 还有一个小脑袋。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So both those statues and the statue in Deptford was set up at the beginning of the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 所以这两尊雕像，还有德普福德的那尊雕像，都是在21世纪初建立的。

sentences.en: And Putin, when he came to London, went to visit it and he was escorted by Prince Andrew.
sentences.zh: 普京来到伦敦时，曾去参观它，并由安德鲁王子陪同。

sentences.en: Oh, my word.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: There's a couple.
sentences.zh: 这真是一对绝配。

sentences.en: There's an interesting episode from history.
sentences.zh: 这是一个历史上的有趣片段。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I looked up what it actually said on the statue and it said, this monument is erected near the Royal Shipyard where Peter the Great studied the English science of shipbuilding.
sentences.zh: 所以我查了查雕像上到底写了什么，上面写着：“这座纪念碑竖立在皇家造船厂附近，彼得大帝曾在这里学习英国的造船科学。”

sentences.en: The monument is a gift from the Russian people and commemorates the visit of Peter the Great to this country in search of knowledge and experience.
sentences.zh: “该纪念碑是俄罗斯人民的礼物，旨在纪念彼得大帝为寻求知识和经验而对这个国家进行的访问。”

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: So that's nice.
sentences.zh: 所以这挺不错的。

sentences.en: Well, Peter did get knowledge and experience, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 好吧，公平地说，彼得确实学到了知识和经验。

sentences.en: I'll tell you one thing he picked up was smoking.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你他学会的一件事就是抽烟。

sentences.en: Smoking previously banned in Russia, except in the German suburb.
sentences.zh: 吸烟此前在俄罗斯是被禁止的，德国人聚居区除外。

sentences.en: He signs a deal with this bloke, Carmarthen, that he goes drinking with so that Carmarthen can import tobacco to Russia.
sentences.zh: 他与经常一起喝酒的家伙卡马森达成了一笔交易，以便卡马森能够将烟草进口到俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And also, he does manage to get about 60 mathematicians, shipwrights, engineers, and he persuades them to come back with him to Russia, as well as to Barber's right.
sentences.zh: 而且，他还真的拉到了大约60名数学家、造船工、工程师，说服他们跟他一起回俄罗斯，还有理发师。

sentences.en: So his westernizing brain is ticking over.
sentences.zh: 所以他那西化的头脑正在飞速运转。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So 2nd of May, he says, look, I've been here for ages.
sentences.zh: 所以在5月2日，他说，听着，我在这里待得够久了。

sentences.en: It's time to go on.
sentences.zh: 是时候继续前行了。

sentences.en: He loved England.
sentences.zh: 他热爱英国。

sentences.en: And we're used to the Russians being incredibly disobliging about our beloved country, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 我们习惯了俄罗斯人对我们深爱的国家表现得极其不客气，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, wealthy Russians, they tend to like London.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，富有的俄罗斯人，他们往往喜欢伦敦。

sentences.en: They like our football clubs.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢我们的足球俱乐部。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They like our bijou West End houses.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢我们在西区的精致住宅。

sentences.en: Nationalist commentators were always going on Russian state television, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 民族主义评论员不是总是在俄罗斯国家电视台滔滔不绝吗？

sentences.en: And sort of doing mock-ups of how Britain would be annihilated by a nuclear weapon.
sentences.zh: 然后搞一些英国将被核武器消灭的模拟演示。

sentences.en: Or a tsunami.
sentences.zh: 或者海啸。

sentences.en: Or a tsunami, exactly.
sentences.zh: 或者海啸，完全没错。

sentences.en: But Peter the Great would not have approved of that, because he told a captain later, he said it would be a much happier life to be an admiral in England than a czar in Russia.
sentences.zh: 但彼得大帝是不会赞同这一点的，因为他后来对一位船长说，在英国当一名海军上将，要比在俄罗斯当沙皇幸福得多。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm so happy to be quoting this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我太高兴能引用这句话了。

sentences.en: He said, England is the best, the most beautiful, and the happiest place on earth.
sentences.zh: 他说，英国是地球上最好、最美丽、最幸福的地方。

sentences.en: So although he's a brutal and murderous autocrat, he's clearly not all bad.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管他是一个残暴嗜杀的独裁者，但他显然并非一无是处。

sentences.en: No, he's a man of tremendous taste.
sentences.zh: 不，他是一个极有品味的人。

sentences.en: Now, sadly, not all Englishmen are as keen on Peter the Great as he is on them, because as soon as he's left, John Evelyn goes to see what's happened to his house.
sentences.zh: 现在，遗憾的是，并非所有英国人都像他对他们那样对彼得大帝充满热情，因为他一离开，约翰·伊夫林就去查看他的房子变成了什么样。

sentences.en: And it is most nasty.
sentences.zh: 结果简直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And it was very nasty.
sentences.zh: 而且确实非常糟糕。

sentences.en: He's so appalled.
sentences.zh: 他震惊万分。

sentences.en: He then goes straight to the royal surveyor, Sir Christopher Wren, and the royal gardener, who's a man called Mr. London.
sentences.zh: 他随即径直去找皇家测量师克里斯托弗·雷恩爵士和皇家园丁（一个叫伦敦先生的人）。

sentences.en: And he says, come to my house immediately.
sentences.zh: 他说，马上来我家。

sentences.en: The government's going to have to compensate me for this.
sentences.zh: 政府必须为此赔偿我。

sentences.en: And when they get there, they find it has been utterly trashed, ink everywhere, grease everywhere, all the doorknobs and locks have been pried off, the windows have been smashed,
sentences.zh: 当他们到达那里时，发现房子已经被彻底砸烂了，到处都是墨水，到处都是油脂，所有的门把手和锁都被撬了下来，窗户被砸碎了，

sentences.en: the chairs have all been smashed up and used as firewood, the pictures have been ripped up, and the garden, Evelyn's pride and joy, the greatest garden in England,
sentences.zh: 椅子全被砸碎当成了柴火，画作被撕破了，而那个花园——伊夫林的骄傲与欢乐、英格兰最伟大的花园——

sentences.en: absolutely destroyed.
sentences.zh: 被彻底摧毁了。

sentences.en: The claim is, I think there's some dispute among scholars about whether this is invented or not, that they'd been having wheelbarrow races through the hedges.
sentences.zh: 有传言说——我想学者们对这是否是虚构的还有些争论——他们曾在树篱间进行过独轮车比赛。

sentences.en: So, to quote, the lawn was trampled into mud and dust as if a regiment of soldiers in iron shoes had drilled on it.
sentences.zh: 所以，借用原话，“草坪被踩踏成泥泞和尘土，仿佛一团穿着铁鞋的士兵连队在上面进行过演练。”

sentences.en: And who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I mean, Peter loves a fake army, so maybe they'd done that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，彼得热爱虚构的军队，所以也许他们真的那样做过。

sentences.en: The magnificent holly hedge had been flattened by wheelbarrows rammed through it.
sentences.zh: 那壮丽的冬青树篱也被横冲直撞的独轮车给压平了。

sentences.en: So, presumably, that's where that story comes from.
sentences.zh: 所以，想必这就是那个故事的由来吧。
