sentences.en: more than a million pounds today that Evelyn was given as compensation.
sentences.zh: 伊芙琳得到的补偿相当于如今的一百多万英镑。

sentences.en: That tells you just how much damage there was.
sentences.zh: 这说明当时遭到的破坏有多么严重。

sentences.en: So, Peter, by now, is long gone.
sentences.zh: 所以，此时的彼得早就离开了。

sentences.en: He goes to Dresden.
sentences.zh: 他去了德累斯顿。

sentences.en: He goes to Vienna.
sentences.zh: 他去了维也纳。

sentences.en: And Dominic, in Dresden, crucially, he sees the Kunstkammer Museum, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而在德累斯顿，多米尼克最关键的是参观了艺术珍品陈列馆，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Which is a cabinet of curiosities.
sentences.zh: 那是一个奇珍异宝柜。

sentences.en: And so, we talked about how, in the Netherlands, Peter had seen ways to preserve corpses.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们之前聊过彼得在荷兰是如何看到保存尸体的方法的。

sentences.en: And now, he's seen a cabinet of curiosities.
sentences.zh: 现在，他又见识了奇珍异宝柜。

sentences.en: And this is setting up, again, all kinds of ideas in his fertile and faintly dark brain.
sentences.zh: 这再次激发了他那丰富又略带阴暗的大脑中的各种奇思妙想。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, he has a nice time in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 总之，他在维也纳过得很愉快。

sentences.en: And then he's preparing to move on to Venice in July when bombshell news.
sentences.zh: 正当他准备在7月份动身前往威尼斯时，惊天消息传来了。

sentences.en: He has a letter from Moscow from his mate, Romadonovsky.
sentences.zh: 他收到了来自莫斯科的信，寄信人是他的密友罗马诺夫斯基。

sentences.en: Terrible things have been happening in Russia.
sentences.zh: 俄国发生了可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Four regiments of Streltsy were being transferred from the Sea of Azov to the Polish frontier.
sentences.zh: 斯特列尔齐近卫军的四个团正从亚速海调往波兰边境。

sentences.en: And they have mutinied.
sentences.zh: 他们哗变了。

sentences.en: They are now marching on Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他们现在正向莫斯科进军。

sentences.en: And they're only 60 miles away.
sentences.zh: 而且距离只有60英里了。

sentences.en: And, of course, this letter has taken a long time to reach Peter.
sentences.zh: 当然，这封信送到彼得手里花了很长时间。

sentences.en: Peter can't believe it.
sentences.zh: 彼得简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: So, what this means is that while he's been messing around with cabinets of curiosities in Dresden and dancing at balls in Vienna, the Streltsy may well have taken Moscow.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，当他还在德累斯顿摆弄奇珍异宝柜、在维也纳的舞会上跳舞时，斯特列尔齐近卫军很可能已经攻占了莫斯科。

sentences.en: He may have been deposed and proclaimed a traitor.
sentences.zh: 他可能已经被废黜并被宣布为叛国者。

sentences.en: He says, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 他说，天哪。

sentences.en: So, he scraps his plan.
sentences.zh: 于是，他取消了计划。

sentences.en: The gap year is over.
sentences.zh: 间隔年结束了。

sentences.en: And he rushes eaSt.
sentences.zh: 他火速赶往东方。

sentences.en: And he's riding through Poland day and night, stopping only to change horses.
sentences.zh: 他在波兰境内日夜骑马赶路，除了换马之外绝不停留。

sentences.en: And then he gets to Krakow.
sentences.zh: 然后他到达了克拉科夫。

sentences.en: And another messenger comes riding up from the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 另一个信使从东方策马赶来。

sentences.en: And Peter sort of rips open the message.
sentences.zh: 彼得一把撕开信件。

sentences.en: A massive sigh of relief.
sentences.zh: 如释重负地长出一口气。

sentences.en: Romadonovsky reports that their troops have intercepted and defeated the Streltsy rebels.
sentences.zh: 罗马诺夫斯基报告说，他们的军队已经拦截并击败了斯特列尔齐叛军。

sentences.en: Although he's going to carry on going home, he can slow down a bit.
sentences.zh: 虽然他还是要回家，但步伐可以稍微放慢一点了。

sentences.en: And he heads to meet somebody who will play a big part in the story, who is Augustus the Strong.
sentences.zh: 于是他去见了一个在这段历史中扮演重要角色的人，也就是强力王奥古斯特。

sentences.en: And you love him, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你很喜欢他，对吧？

sentences.en: I love Augustus the Strong.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢强力王奥古斯特了。

sentences.en: He's one of your favourite characters from all of history.
sentences.zh: 他是你最喜欢的历史人物之一。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实是的。

sentences.en: So, he was the elector of Saxony, Augustus.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯特是萨克森选帝侯。

sentences.en: And he'd been elected King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania in 1698.
sentences.zh: 他在1698年被选为波兰国王兼立陶宛大公。

sentences.en: And we said we'd get into the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
sentences.zh: 我们说过要聊聊波兰立陶宛联邦。

sentences.en: It's this great sort of ramshackle state of 8 million people.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由800万人口组成的庞大而散漫的国家。

sentences.en: Vast, culturally fascinating.
sentences.zh: 幅员辽阔，文化迷人。

sentences.en: A real mix of Catholics, Jews and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 天主教徒、犹太人以及各种各样的人真正融合在一起。

sentences.en: Fascinating kind of mosaic.
sentences.zh: 一种迷人的马赛克拼图般的国家。

sentences.en: Even MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有穆斯林。

sentences.en: Even Muslims, exactly.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有穆斯林，没错。

sentences.en: Because there are Muslims who've been settled there.
sentences.zh: 因为那里定居着一些穆斯林。

sentences.en: Sort of heretics of various kinds go there because it's so tolerant.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的异教徒也去那里，因为那里非常包容。

sentences.en: It's sort of an experiment in multiculturalism in some ways.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，它有点像多元文化主义的实验。

sentences.en: But it's beginning to fall apart a bit.
sentences.zh: 但它开始有点分崩离析了。

sentences.en: And it's got a bonkers political system.
sentences.zh: 而且它的政治体制极其荒诞。

sentences.en: Because diversity is not necessarily its strength.
sentences.zh: 因为多样性未必就是它的力量源泉。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这样说挺公道的。

sentences.en: Now, Augustus has been elected to rule this kingdom.
sentences.zh: 现在，奥古斯特被选为这个王国的统治者。

sentences.en: He's a gigantic man like Peter.
sentences.zh: 他像彼得一样是个身材高大的人。

sentences.en: He looks like a bear.
sentences.zh: 他长得像头熊。

sentences.en: His party trick.
sentences.zh: 他的招牌绝技。

sentences.en: Well, he has multiple party tricks.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他有很多招牌绝技。

sentences.en: He likes to amuse his courtiers by snapping horseshoes with one hand.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢单手捏断马蹄铁来取悦他的朝臣。

sentences.en: I don't know how you do that, but he does it anyway.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是怎么做到的，反正他就是能做到。

sentences.en: Presumably with fingers.
sentences.zh: 大概是用手指吧。

sentences.en: It's a reflection on the strength of his fingers, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想这反映了他手指的力量。

sentences.en: His fingers.
sentences.zh: 他的手指。

sentences.en: You could just snap your fingers and snap a horseshoe.
sentences.zh: 你只要打个响指就能捏断马蹄铁。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: If you're just doing it with one hand.
sentences.zh: 如果你只用一只手的话。

sentences.en: He loves collecting porcelain.
sentences.zh: 他热爱收集瓷器。

sentences.en: He has dozens of mistresses.
sentences.zh: 他有几十个情妇。

sentences.en: He fathered 354 illegitimate children, which I think is a lot.
sentences.zh: 他生了354个私生子，我觉得这数量相当惊人。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: He collected lions, hyenas, monkeys, and meerkats.
sentences.zh: 他收集狮子、鬣狗、猴子和猫鼬。

sentences.en: Meerkats?
sentences.zh: 猫鼬？

sentences.en: Yeah, meerkats.
sentences.zh: 对，猫鼬。

sentences.en: Is he the first European royal to collect a meerkat?
sentences.zh: 他是第一个收集猫鼬的欧洲皇室成员吗？

sentences.en: I think he probably is.
sentences.zh: 我想他大概是的。

sentences.en: They were always shipping animals to him, and they'd open the box, and the animal would be dead.
sentences.zh: 人们总是把动物运送给他，等他们打开箱子时，动物往往已经死了。

sentences.en: That was the usual scenario.
sentences.zh: 这通常都是这个结果。

sentences.en: It was pretty tough on the animals.
sentences.zh: 这对动物来说太惨了。

sentences.en: And he's not one of history's great animal lovers, because his real party piece, his specialism, the thing for which he goes down in history,
sentences.zh: 而且他并不是历史上伟大的动物爱好者，因为他的拿手好戏、他的绝活、他名留青史的事迹，

sentences.en: is he's probably history's most proficient fox tosser.
sentences.zh: 是他可能是历史上最高产的“掷狐狸”高手。

sentences.en: So, if you're interested in tossing a fox, Augustus the Strong is the absolute model.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对掷狐狸感兴趣，强力王奥古斯特绝对是典范。

sentences.en: So, once, when he was receiving the King of Prussia, to greet the King of Prussia, he tossed 200 foxes, six wildcats, two badgers, and two beavers.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他在接待普鲁士国王时，为了迎接普鲁士国王，他抛掷了200只狐狸、6只野猫、2只獾和2只海狸。

sentences.en: And when I say tossed, he tossed them to their deaths.
sentences.zh: 我说的抛掷，是指把它们抛向死亡。

sentences.en: That's what he does.
sentences.zh: 他就是这么干的。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So, basically, his servants will line up with these beavers and badgers.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他的仆人们会带着这些海狸和獾排好队。

sentences.en: He just grabs them, throws them up in the air.
sentences.zh: 他抓起它们，往空中一扔。

sentences.en: Throws them in the air?
sentences.zh: 往空中扔？

sentences.en: So high that they come crashing down to earth and die.
sentences.zh: 扔得那么高，以至于它们重重地摔在地上惨死。

sentences.en: He's like, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 他就觉得，太棒了。

sentences.en: So, he doesn't catch them?
sentences.zh: 所以他不接住它们？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不接。

sentences.en: Are they splattered over the ceiling?
sentences.zh: 难道它们血溅天花板吗？

sentences.en: Surely he does this outdoors.
sentences.zh: 他肯定是在户外的吧。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, you go into the garden.
sentences.zh: 所以你走到花园里。

sentences.en: There's a menagerie there all lined up.
sentences.zh: 那里排好了各种珍禽异兽。

sentences.en: And everyone applauds politely.
sentences.zh: 然后大家都礼貌地鼓掌。

sentences.en: Augustus the Strong is just throwing foxes around.
sentences.zh: 强力王奥古斯特就在那儿把狐狸扔来扔去。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems bonkers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Hurrah for your majesty.
sentences.zh: 为陛下欢呼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: In the late 17th, early 18th century, this is very high-class entertainment.
sentences.zh: 在17世纪末18世纪初，这可是非常高档的娱乐活动。

sentences.en: So, don't knock it.
sentences.zh: 所以别瞧不起它。

sentences.en: And actually, to be fair, let's not knock it until we've done it, because we've never tried it or seen it.
sentences.zh: 说实话，在我们亲身体验或亲眼目睹之前，还是先别妄加非议了，因为我们从来没试过也没看过。

sentences.en: Peter loves this.
sentences.zh: 彼得对这个爱不释手。

sentences.en: Of course, he does.
sentences.zh: 当然了，他肯定喜欢。

sentences.en: Very much his thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这非常符合他的风格，对吧？

sentences.en: Augustus the Strong will throw a beaver to his death.
sentences.zh: 强力王奥古斯特会把海狸扔死。

sentences.en: And then, Peter will kiss him and say, oh, you're brilliant.
sentences.zh: 然后，彼得会亲吻他并说，哦，你太棒了。

sentences.en: I love this.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: I love you.
sentences.zh: 我爱你。

sentences.en: Does Peter have a go at fox tossing?
sentences.zh: 彼得自己也试过掷狐狸吗？

sentences.en: I don't know that he does, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我不知道他有没有试过。

sentences.en: Maybe he would use his bellows or something.
sentences.zh: 也许他会用他的风箱什么的吧。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems very much his kind of sport.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来非常符合他的运动爱好。

sentences.en: I'd like to think he'd tried his hand at it, wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 你也会希望他曾经亲手尝试过吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He'd try to toss a bear, probably, knowing him.
sentences.zh: 了解他的话，他可能会尝试去扔一头熊。

sentences.en: Peter said to his nobleman, I prize Augustus more than the whole of you put together, not because he's a king, but merely because I like him.
sentences.zh: 彼得对他的贵族们说，我珍视奥古斯特胜过你们所有人的总和，不是因为他是国王，而仅仅是因为我喜欢他。

sentences.en: Which is quite sweet.
sentences.zh: 这话挺暖心的。

sentences.en: And actually, in between killing all these animals, Augustus takes the opportunity to pitch an idea to Peter that will have massive, massive long-term political consequences.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在杀完这些动物的间隙，奥古斯特趁机向彼得提出一个将产生巨大且深远政治影响的想法。

sentences.en: Because both of them hate and fear their northern neighbours, the Swedes.
sentences.zh: 因为他们俩都极其痛恨和恐惧北方的邻居瑞典人。

sentences.en: They can't stand the Swedes.
sentences.zh: 他们对瑞典人恨之入骨。

sentences.en: The Swedes, the most formidable and modern military power in northern Europe.
sentences.zh: 瑞典人是北欧最强大、最现代化的军事力量。

sentences.en: And Augustus says, listen, the Swedish king has died, and his successor, who's a bloke called Charles XII, he's a total nobody.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯特说，听着，瑞典国王已经死了，他的继任者是个叫查理十二世的小子，根本无足轻重。

sentences.en: He's only 15.
sentences.zh: 他才15岁。

sentences.en: He's a teenager.
sentences.zh: 他还是个青少年。

sentences.en: Let's join forces against the Swedes and divide up their Baltic empire between us.
sentences.zh: 让我们联手对付瑞典人，把他们在波罗的海的帝国瓜分了吧。

sentences.en: And Peter, who we know loves Augustus the Strong, says, do you know, that sounds brilliant.
sentences.zh: 而我们深知喜爱强力王奥古斯特的彼得则说，你知道吗，这听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: Because actually, my war against the Ottomans is a complete non-event.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，我对奥斯曼帝国的战争完全没取得什么进展。

sentences.en: Total damp squib.
sentences.zh: 雷声大雨点小。

sentences.en: I'm never going to beat the Ottomans.
sentences.zh: 我永远也打败不了奥斯曼人。

sentences.en: Forget the back sea, and we'll move on to the Baltic.
sentences.zh: 忘掉黑海吧，我们把目标转向波罗的海。

sentences.en: Let's keep working on this idea, and one day, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 让我们继续完善这个构想，总有一天，我们要把它付诸行动。

sentences.en: Now, in the meantime, he has to go back to Moscow, which he does.
sentences.zh: 眼下，他不得不返回莫斯科，他也确实这么做了。

sentences.en: He goes back to Moscow with all his kind of shipwrights and whatnot, and all his sort of, he's fired with enthusiasm for his westernizing project.
sentences.zh: 他带着他的一帮造船工和其他随从回到了莫斯科，他心中对西化大业充满了狂热的激情。

sentences.en: He goes to his estate at Praia-Brazhanskoye.
sentences.zh: 他回到了他在普列奥布拉任斯科耶的庄园。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: I was looking forward to that.
sentences.zh: 我一直很期待这一刻。

sentences.en: I could see it looming in the notes.
sentences.zh: 我看到它在笔记里若隐若现了。

sentences.en: I thought, okay, I've just got to go for it.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，我必须豁出去了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he arrives on the night of the 4th of September, 1698.
sentences.zh: 他于1698年9月4日夜里抵达。

sentences.en: And the next day, the 5th, all his noblemen say, oh, brilliant, you're back.
sentences.zh: 第二天，也就是9月5日，所有贵族都跑来对他说，哦，太棒了，你回来了。

sentences.en: They come to go and greet him.
sentences.zh: 他们前来迎接他。

sentences.en: He embraces them.
sentences.zh: 他拥抱他们。

sentences.en: He kisses them.
sentences.zh: 他亲吻他们。

sentences.en: And then out of his back pocket, he pulls out a razor.
sentences.zh: 接着，他从后口袋里掏出一把剃刀。

sentences.en: And then just starts shaving them, cutting off their beards.
sentences.zh: 然后直接开始帮他们刮胡子，把他们的胡须割掉。

sentences.en: They are so stunned, they don't know how to react.
sentences.zh: 他们震惊得不知所措，完全不知道该作何反应。

sentences.en: And he's like very violently, forcibly shaving them.
sentences.zh: 而且他动作非常暴力、强硬地给他们刮胡子。

sentences.en: Now, the thing is, we did a whole episode, didn't we, about beards and about this business.
sentences.zh: 有一说一，我们之前做过整整一期节目，对吧，讲的就是胡须和这档子事。

sentences.en: And for people who missed it, to very briefly explain, to Orthodox Russians, the beard was a gift from God.
sentences.zh: 为了给没听过的听众简单解释一下，在正统俄罗斯人看来，胡须是上帝赐予的礼物。

sentences.en: And to shave it was a sin.
sentences.zh: 刮胡子就是一种罪孽。

sentences.en: Ivan the Terrible had specifically said, it's a sin that the blood of all the martyrs cannot cleanse because it is to deface the image of man created by God.
sentences.zh: 伊凡雷霆曾明确说过，这是一种连所有殉道者的鲜血都无法洗刷的罪过，因为这是在亵渎上帝创造的人类形象。

sentences.en: And Peter says, no, this is nonsense, a beard is backwards.
sentences.zh: 而彼得却说，胡扯，胡须是落后的象征。

sentences.en: And he makes everybody shave off their beards.
sentences.zh: 他强迫所有人都刮掉胡子。

sentences.en: And in the long run, if you want to have a beard, you have to pay a special tax and you get a medallion with a picture of a beard on it.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，如果你非要留胡须，就得缴纳一笔特殊的税，然后你会得到一枚印有胡须图案的奖章。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: And then you're allowed to have a beard.
sentences.zh: 这样你才被允许留胡子。

sentences.en: And this is just one of a host of changes.
sentences.zh: 而这只是无数变革中的一项。

sentences.en: So basically, up to this point, Russian noblemen had worn these caftans, floppy coloured boots, very exotic garb.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，在此之前，俄罗斯贵族一直穿着长袍、宽松的花色靴子，以及非常异域风情的服装。

sentences.en: But also appropriate to the cold weather.
sentences.zh: 不过这也确实适合寒冷的天气。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it does keep you warm, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实保暖，对吧？

sentences.en: So layers, they believe in layers.
sentences.zh: 所以他们崇尚叠穿，层层保暖。

sentences.en: Peter does not believe in that.
sentences.zh: 彼得可不买账。

sentences.en: He says, this is backwards.
sentences.zh: 他说，这太落后了。

sentences.en: Again, it's Asiatic.
sentences.zh: 这同样是亚洲作风。

sentences.en: It's not right.
sentences.zh: 这不对劲。

sentences.en: He cuts the sleeves of people's robes off.
sentences.zh: 他直接把别人长袍的袖子给剪了。

sentences.en: Like you turn up to a state reception or something.
sentences.zh: 就像你盛装出席国宴或者别的什么场合一样。

sentences.en: Peter the Great will come at you with a razor and a pair of scissors, probably Dutch or English scissors.
sentences.zh: 彼得大帝会带着剃刀和一把剪刀向你走来，大概是荷兰或英国造的剪刀。

sentences.en: And we'll be cutting off bits of your clothing.
sentences.zh: 然后把你的衣服剪得七零八落。

sentences.en: He says, I want people to wear what they call French or German style coats.
sentences.zh: 他说，我希望人们穿他们所谓法式或德式风格的外套。

sentences.en: He says, I want to see waistcoats.
sentences.zh: 他说，我希望看到马甲。

sentences.en: I want to see breeches.
sentences.zh: 我希望看到紧身马裤。

sentences.en: I want women to wear bonnets and skirts, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我希望女性戴软帽、穿裙子，诸如此类。

sentences.en: What about corsets?
sentences.zh: 那紧身胸衣呢？

sentences.en: If you go to Moscow, they hang up models of the approved costumes.
sentences.zh: 如果你去莫斯科，会看到那里挂着获准服装的样衣。

sentences.en: And Peter says, when people are coming into the city, the guards have to have pairs of scissors as well.
sentences.zh: 彼得下令，当人们进城时，守卫也必须随身携带剪刀。

sentences.en: And if people are wearing long caftans, the guards will cut the snip, snip, snip, snip, snip, exactly.
sentences.zh: 如果有人穿着长袍，守卫就会咔嚓、咔嚓、咔嚓、咔嚓地剪掉，就是这样。

sentences.en: So it obviously didn't work among the great mass of the population at all.
sentences.zh: 所以这在广大底层民众中显然根本行不通。

sentences.en: But among the elite, it did.
sentences.zh: 但在精英阶层中，确实推行下去了。

sentences.en: Because foreign ambassadors say that by the middle of the sort of first decade of the 18th century, at balls and at banquets and things,
sentences.zh: 因为外国大使说，到18世纪第一个十年的中期左右，在舞会、宴会以及各种场合上，

sentences.en: people will be dressing in the German manner.
sentences.zh: 人们都已经穿上了德式服饰。

sentences.en: It must have been so cold, though.
sentences.zh: 不过那一定冷得够呛吧。

sentences.en: Imagine, you know, your stockings and your britches and the icy wind from the Urals.
sentences.zh: 试想一下，穿着长袜和紧身马裤，还要顶着来自乌拉尔山的冰冷刺骨的寒风。

sentences.en: Yeah, but that's fine.
sentences.zh: 对，但没关系。

sentences.en: But I mean, would you rather do that or would you rather take your chances with Peter the Great, a razor, scissors?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是愿意这么做，还是愿意去跟彼得大帝、剃刀和剪刀硬碰硬？

sentences.en: No, I wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 不，我才不呢。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an invidious choice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个两难的选择。

sentences.en: It's not the only thing he changes.
sentences.zh: 这可不是他改变的唯一一件事。

sentences.en: He changes the calendar.
sentences.zh: 他还改了历法。

sentences.en: So up till this point, the Russians have dated time from the creation of the world.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，俄罗斯人是以世界创造之年作为纪元起点的。

sentences.en: And Peter says, well, that's rubbish.
sentences.zh: 彼得说，这简直一派胡言。

sentences.en: Let's do it from Jesus's birth like everybody else does in Europe.
sentences.zh: 咱们跟欧洲其他国家一样，从耶稣诞生开始记年吧。

sentences.en: So they adopt the Julian calendar.
sentences.zh: 于是他们采用了儒略历。

sentences.en: They don't really have very good coinage.
sentences.zh: 他们当时并没有很好的铸币系统。

sentences.en: They were just using bits of other people's coins.
sentences.zh: 他们只是拿别人的硬币碎块来用。

sentences.en: They'd kind of cut up.
sentences.zh: 把它们切割开来。

sentences.en: And he says, come on.
sentences.zh: 于是他说，拜托。

sentences.en: He loves the English coinage.
sentences.zh: 他特别喜欢英国的硬币。

sentences.en: Because he'd studied the mint, hadn't he, in the Tower of London?
sentences.zh: 因为他参观并研究过伦敦塔的铸币厂，不是吗？

sentences.en: He'd been to the mint.
sentences.zh: 他去过铸币厂。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He says, you must have coinage just like the English do.
sentences.zh: 他说，你们必须拥有和英国人一样的铸币。

sentences.en: Now, for him personally, there's a big change as well.
sentences.zh: 现在，对他个人而言，也发生了一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: And all the time he'd been gone, 18 months, he had not written once to his wife, Eudokia.
sentences.zh: 在他离家的这漫长18个月里，他一次也没有给妻子叶夫多基娅写过信。

sentences.en: So people may remember from the last episode, she's pink.
sentences.zh: 大家可能还记得上一集的内容，她是个浅薄无知的人。

sentences.en: Yes, pink, hopeless and helpless, I think was the description.
sentences.zh: 没错，浅薄、无望且无助，我想当时的形容就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He sees her as the embodiment of conservatism and orthodoxy.
sentences.zh: 在他眼里，她是保守主义和东正教传统的化身。

sentences.en: And while he's been away, he's obviously thought to himself, I can't stand her.
sentences.zh: 而他在外出的这段时间里，心里肯定在想：我受够她了。

sentences.en: She's got to go.
sentences.zh: 她必须得走。

sentences.en: So he basically summons her.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是把她传唤了过来。

sentences.en: She's like, oh, great, you're home.
sentences.zh: 她当时还想，哦太好了，你回家啦。

sentences.en: And he says, well, I am.
sentences.zh: 结果他说，我是回来了。

sentences.en: But you've got to go, I'm afraid.
sentences.zh: 但恐怕你得走了。

sentences.en: You're off to a nunnery.
sentences.zh: 你得去修道院了。

sentences.en: And he takes his son, Alexis, from her and gives him to his sister.
sentences.zh: 接着他从她身边夺走了他们的儿子阿列克谢，交给了自己的姐姐抚养。

sentences.en: And this, as we will see in our final episode of this series, is a very traumatic moment for young Alexis.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在本系列最后一集里将要看到的，这对年幼的阿列克谢来说是一个极其痛苦的时刻。

sentences.en: And their relationship will be difficult, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我想客观地说，他们父子俩的关系日后将会非常艰难。

sentences.en: But it's so interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这实在太有趣了，不是吗？

sentences.en: We've had so many series recently where unwanted women get packed off to nunneries.
sentences.zh: 最近我们看过好几个系列，里面那些不受欢迎的女人都被打发去了修道院。

sentences.en: So it happened in our series on the Franks, it happened in our series on the road to 1066.
sentences.zh: 我们在讲法兰克人的系列里看到过，在讲通往1066之路的系列里也看到过。

sentences.en: We've also had Japanese women going off and becoming nuns.
sentences.zh: 我们还讲过日本女性出家当尼姑的故事。

sentences.en: So very much a theme.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是一个常见的母题。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And poor old Yudokia, she was forced into a carriage and sent to a convent in Susdal and her head was shaved.
sentences.zh: 可怜的叶夫多基娅被强行塞进马车，送到苏兹达尔的一座修道院，还被剃光了头发。

sentences.en: So like the Japanese.
sentences.zh: 就像日本人那样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: And she was renamed Helen and she had to become a nun with the name of Helen.
sentences.zh: 她被改名为叶莲娜，被迫以叶莲娜这个名字当了修女。

sentences.en: Now, of course, he has come home because he's heard about this mutiny among the Streltsi.
sentences.zh: 当然啦，他这次回国是因为听说了斯特列利茨基近卫军哗变的消息。

sentences.en: The people who had, you know, carried out that horrendous massacre in front of him when he was 10 years old.
sentences.zh: 就是当年他十岁时，在他眼前制造了那场惨绝人寰大屠杀的那群人。

sentences.en: And he is clearly determined that he will use this as a pretext to finish them off forever.
sentences.zh: 他显然下定决心，要以此为借口彻底消灭他们。

sentences.en: However, there's a really a paranoid side, I think, to Peter.
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为彼得性格中确实有着多疑的一面。

sentences.en: He reminds me of Henry VIII, you know, in insecurity.
sentences.zh: 他在不安全感这方面让我想起了亨利八世。

sentences.en: In Henry VIII's case, I guess it's because, you know, his father won the throne at Bosworth on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 就亨利八世而言，我猜那是因为他的父亲是在博斯沃思战场上赢得王位的。

sentences.en: And he's always worried about the dynasty.
sentences.zh: 所以他总是担心王朝的统治不稳。

sentences.en: In Peter's case, it's because he had to fight.
sentences.zh: 而在彼得的例子中，是因为他不得不一路苦战才夺得权力。

sentences.en: I mean, just because you're paranoid doesn't mean people aren't out to get you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，哪怕你疑神疑鬼，也不代表别人不想害你。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he is determined to make a massive example of the mutineers and to show that it was.
sentences.zh: 他决心拿这些叛乱分子杀鸡儆猴，以儆效尤。

sentences.en: He believes that this is part of a massive conspiracy orchestrated by his sister, Sophia, who's, of course, in a nunnery herself.
sentences.zh: 他坚信这是由他姐姐索菲亚精心策划的大规模阴谋的一部分，而索菲亚当然也已经被关在修道院里了。

sentences.en: And so he has all the mutineers brought to his estate at Praia Brazanskoye.
sentences.zh: 于是，他把所有的叛乱分子都押到了他在普列奥布拉任斯科耶的庄园。

sentences.en: There you go, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好样的，汤姆。

sentences.en: That's so good.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Loving it.
sentences.zh: 我太爱了。

sentences.en: I'm just going to do it unnecessarily now, even when it's not relevant.
sentences.zh: 我甚至要在不必要的时候、在毫不相关的情况下也这么来一句。

sentences.en: I'm probably not even pronouncing it correctly, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我可能连发音都不太对。

sentences.en: And at his estate, this is the dark side of Peter.
sentences.zh: 而在他的庄园里，展现出了彼得黑暗的一面。

sentences.en: He commissions his men to build 14 special torture chambers.
sentences.zh: 他命令手下建造了14间专门的酷刑室。

sentences.en: So they bring the mutineers.
sentences.zh: 他们把叛乱分子押了过来。

sentences.en: And every week, for six days a week, the Streltsy mutineers are interrogated.
sentences.zh: 每周有六天，斯特列利茨基近卫军的叛变者们都会遭到审讯。

sentences.en: They are beaten with sticks.
sentences.zh: 他们被棍棒殴打。

sentences.en: They're roasted over open fires.
sentences.zh: 他们在明火上炙烤。

sentences.en: And above all, they are lashed with a thing called the knout, which is this massive leather whip.
sentences.zh: 最可怕的是，他们被一种叫作“克瑙特”的巨型皮鞭抽打。

sentences.en: 25 strokes of the knout will kill you.
sentences.zh: 挨上25下这种皮鞭就会要了你的命。

sentences.en: And it literally kind of rips the skin from your back.
sentences.zh: 它简直能把你的后背活活撕下一层皮。

sentences.en: And it's kind of like an assembly line.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一条流水线。

sentences.en: And Peter and his friends and his cronies and his jolly company are the people doing the torturing.
sentences.zh: 而彼得、他的朋友们、亲信们以及他那群酒肉朋友就是行刑的人。

sentences.en: So not so jolly now.
sentences.zh: 现在可一点也不好玩了。

sentences.en: Not jolly now.
sentences.zh: 一点也不好玩了。

sentences.en: And he would absolutely join in.
sentences.zh: 而且他绝对会亲自加入。

sentences.en: And he will be beating these people with an ivory-handled cane.
sentences.zh: 他会用一根镶着象牙柄的手杖殴打这些人。

sentences.en: And it's so violent that the patriarch actually says to Peter, this is too much.
sentences.zh: 场面极其残暴，以至于大牧首实在看下去，对彼得说，这太过了。

sentences.en: Stop.
sentences.zh: 住手吧。

sentences.en: And Peter is livid about this.
sentences.zh: 彼得对此勃然大怒。

sentences.en: And he says to the patriarch, no, Russian society is infected with the disease and I am burning it out.
sentences.zh: 他对大牧首说，不，俄罗斯社会已经病入膏肓，我正在把它付之一炬彻底根除。

sentences.en: And actually, what he gets out of the Streltsy, they confess and they say, we'd planned to storm the capital.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他从近卫军那里逼供出了他们的招认，他们供称：我们原本计划攻占首都。

sentences.en: We were going to burn down the German suburb.
sentences.zh: 我们打算烧毁德国人聚居区。

sentences.en: We were going to get rid of the foreigners.
sentences.zh: 我们要赶走外国人。

sentences.en: And we were going to get Sophia to rule over us again.
sentences.zh: 我们还要让索菲亚重新统治我们。

sentences.en: But is there any truth to this?
sentences.zh: 但这些话有哪怕一点真实性吗？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, I guess they're just saying whatever.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得他们大概只是在顺着逼供胡说八道吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're saying what he wants to.
sentences.zh: 对，他们只是在说他想听的话。

sentences.en: Sophia almost certainly didn't know about this.
sentences.zh: 索菲亚几乎可以肯定对此毫不知情。

sentences.en: It's not that she had instigated the plot.
sentences.zh: 并不是她煽动了这场阴谋。

sentences.en: But Peter has never forgiven her.
sentences.zh: 但彼得从未原谅过她。

sentences.en: He goes and interrogates her person who's her convent.
sentences.zh: 他亲自去她所在的修道院审问她。

sentences.en: He says her head must be shaved.
sentences.zh: 他下令必须剃光她的头发。

sentences.en: She must take religious vows and become a nun.
sentences.zh: 她必须发愿皈依宗教并成为一名修女。

sentences.en: And she basically is locked away and is never seen again.
sentences.zh: 她基本上就被终身监禁，再也没有重见天日。

sentences.en: She dies when she's 47, 1704.
sentences.zh: 她在1704年去世，享年47岁。

sentences.en: She had previously, of course, been in the nunnery, but had been relatively well treated.
sentences.zh: 当然，她之前虽然也在修道院里，但待遇相对还算不错。

sentences.en: And now she's effectively a political prisoner.
sentences.zh: 而现在她彻底成了一个政治犯。

sentences.en: And that's not the end of it.
sentences.zh: 但这还远没有结束。

sentences.en: So Peter is determined.
sentences.zh: 所以彼得是铁了心的。

sentences.en: And here, I think you see, you know, loads of countries have a violent history or a history of they have show trials or whatever.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我认为你可以看到，许多国家都有着暴力历史，或者有着搞作秀式审判之类的历史。

sentences.en: I mean, we've done a series on the French Revolution and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们之前做过关于法国大革命之类的系列节目。

sentences.en: But there's a definite theme, I think,
sentences.zh: 不过我认为，在俄罗斯历史上，有一个非常明确的主题

sentences.en: in Russian history of a kind of a fear of enemies within and a conspiracy and a foreign influence and a belief in show trials and public punishment.
sentences.zh: 那就是对内部敌人的恐惧、阴谋、外国影响，以及对作秀审判和公开惩罚的迷信。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, show executions as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有作秀处决。

sentences.en: Show executions.
sentences.zh: 作秀处决。

sentences.en: So he says, well, the Streltsy, you know, they've got to go.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，嗯，斯特列尔齐军，你知道，他们必须得被清除。

sentences.en: And hundreds of them are arrested, brought in in carts to his estate at Preobregen Square.
sentences.zh: 数百人被捕，用马车拉到他在普列奥布拉任斯科耶的庄园。

sentences.en: And they are hanged on a special gibbet in front of a crowd.
sentences.zh: 他们在一个竖立在人群面前的特制绞刑架上被绞死。

sentences.en: Others are beheaded over an open trench.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则在一个露天壕沟上方被斩首。

sentences.en: Quite a few are broken on the wheel, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 相当多的人被施以车裂刑，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is a hideous death.
sentences.zh: 那可是一种可怕的死法。

sentences.en: In Red Square.
sentences.zh: 在红场。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And actually a really sort of chilling thing.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上是一件相当令人不寒栗的事情。

sentences.en: About 200 of them are taken to the convent, Novodovici convent, where Sophia is locked up.
sentences.zh: 大约200人被带到修道院，即索菲亚被关押的新处女修道院。

sentences.en: And Peter has the most prominent members hanged and strung up outside her window.
sentences.zh: 彼得下令将那些最显赫的成员绞死并挂在她窗外。

sentences.en: And they are dangling there.
sentences.zh: 他们就在那里晃荡。

sentences.en: One of them is holding a piece of paper, and that's meant to symbolize their petition that they were going to issue, asking her to rule over them.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人手里拿着一张纸，那是为了象征他们原本要递交的请愿书，请求她来统治他们。

sentences.en: And they are left to hang there outside her window all winter, kind of just dangling, kind of swaying in the wind.
sentences.zh: 他们就这样被留在那儿，整个冬天都挂在她窗外，晃晃悠悠的，在风中摇曳。

sentences.en: And whenever she looks out the window, there they are.
sentences.zh: 每当她向窗外望去，他们就在那里。

sentences.en: I mean, you can only imagine how horrific the sight stench or whatever that must have been for her.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以想象对她来说，那种景象、气味或其他什么是有多可怕。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, that isn't the most shocking thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上，这还不是最令人震惊的事。

sentences.en: Because the most shocking thing is he says he insists that all his friends take part in the executions.
sentences.zh: 因为最令人震惊的是，他说他坚持要所有的朋友都参与行刑。

sentences.en: So there's an Austrian diplomat who actually describes Peter himself wielding the axe, beheading five people, you know, in public, so that everybody can see.
sentences.zh: 所以有一位奥地利外交官描述说，彼得自己挥舞着斧头，当众砍下了五个人的脑袋，好让所有人都看到。

sentences.en: I mean, an incredibly gruesome scene.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个极其恐怖的场面。

sentences.en: So he did it, Dominic, but was he right to do it?
sentences.zh: 所以他这么做了，多米尼克，但他这么做对吗？

sentences.en: Well, Robert K.
sentences.zh: 嗯，罗伯特·K·

sentences.en: Massey, his biographer, he doesn't say he was, but he says this was a public demonstration of Peter's seriousness about his project.
sentences.zh: 马西，他的传记作家，并没有说他做得对，但他认为这是彼得表明其宏伟计划坚定决心的公开展示。

sentences.en: He eliminated the one great obstacle to his modernizing mission, which was the Streltsy.
sentences.zh: 他消除了他现代化使命中的一大障碍，那就是斯特列尔齐军。

sentences.en: And effectively, yeah, he was right to do it.
sentences.zh: 从实际效果来看，是的，他这么做是对的。

sentences.en: That it's a terrible thing, but he was right to do it.
sentences.zh: 尽管这是一件可怕的事情，但他这么做是对的。

sentences.en: I mean, I personally don't think publicly beheading people is the way forward.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我个人认为公开斩首并不是解决问题的好办法。

sentences.en: And leaving corpses dangling outside the cell in which you've imprisoned your sister.
sentences.zh: 而且把尸体挂在你囚禁你姐姐的牢房外面。

sentences.en: No, I wouldn't do that.
sentences.zh: 不，我不会那样做。

sentences.en: So he ends up disbanding the Streltsy completely the year later in 1699.
sentences.zh: 所以他在一年后的1699年彻底解散了斯特列尔齐军。

sentences.en: That leaves him really in a position of absolute power.
sentences.zh: 这真正让他处于绝对权力的地位。

sentences.en: And at first, how does he spend that political capital?
sentences.zh: 起初，他是如何挥霍这些政治资本的呢？

sentences.en: He actually just has endless parties and feasts.
sentences.zh: 他其实只是在没完没了地办派对和宴会。

sentences.en: Huzzah!
sentences.zh: 万岁！

sentences.en: Yeah, so there's a lot of like mad costumes, mocking religious rituals.
sentences.zh: 对，所以有很多疯狂的服装，还有对宗教仪式的嘲弄。

sentences.en: They'll do the sign of the cross with two pipes.
sentences.zh: 他们会用两支烟斗做十字架手势。

sentences.en: Is there bear action?
sentences.zh: 有熊出没吗？

sentences.en: Lots of bears.
sentences.zh: 大量的熊。

sentences.en: Bellows.
sentences.zh: 风箱。

sentences.en: Dwarfs jumping out of pies, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 从馅饼里跳出来的侏儒，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And Peter, often he'll get incredibly drunk, and then he'll have a massive fight with his friends.
sentences.zh: 而且彼得经常喝得烂醉如泥，然后跟他的朋友们大打出手。

sentences.en: I mean, there's stories of him kind of drawing his sword and attacking his friends.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有故事说他拔出剑袭击他的朋友。

sentences.en: He's very, very hot-tempered.
sentences.zh: 他的脾气非常非常暴躁。

sentences.en: I do urge people to watch The Great if they want to see this on a television screen.
sentences.zh: 如果大家想在电视屏幕上看到这一幕，我确实敦促大家去看《凯瑟琳大帝》这部剧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But what's on his mind clearly the whole time is this idea that Augustus the Strong had suggested.
sentences.zh: 但他的脑子里自始至终盘旋着的，显然是强人奥古斯都提出的那个想法。

sentences.en: You know, why don't we have a crack at the Swedes?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们为什么不找瑞典人麻烦呢？

sentences.en: Why don't we try to carve up the Baltic between us?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不试着瓜分波罗的海呢？

sentences.en: Now, the thing is, he's still normally fighting the Ottomans.
sentences.zh: 问题是，他通常还在与奥斯曼人作战。

sentences.en: So he's got to finish that off firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须先完成那件事。

sentences.en: And in July 1700, he agrees a 30-year truce with the Ottomans.
sentences.zh: 在1700年7月，他与奥斯曼人达成了一项为期30年的停战协议。

sentences.en: Peter will keep his conquest at Azov, that we talked about at the beginning of this episode, but he will give up all hope of access to the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 彼得将保留他在本集开头提到的对亚速的征服成果，但他将放弃获得黑海通道的一切希望。

sentences.en: Because now his eye is on the Baltic.
sentences.zh: 因为现在他的目光落在了波罗的海上。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So the news of the treaty reaches Moscow on the 18th of August 1700, and they have a massive fireworks display in celebration.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于这项条约的消息于1700年8月18日传到莫斯科，他们举行了盛大的焰火表演来庆祝。

sentences.en: And the very next day, the 19th of August 1700,
sentences.zh: 就在第二天，即1700年8月19日，

sentences.en: Peter declares war on Sweden.
sentences.zh: 彼得向瑞典宣战。

sentences.en: And with that, the Great Northern War begins.
sentences.zh: 随着这一宣战，大北方战争爆发了。

sentences.en: And for Peter, for Russia, and for the whole of Northern and Eastern Europe, the world will never be the same again.
sentences.zh: 对于彼得、对于俄罗斯，以及对于整个北欧和东欧，世界将永远改变。

sentences.en: And that is an epic story, written on a massive scale.
sentences.zh: 这是一个气势恢弘、规模宏大的史诗般的故事。

sentences.en: And it will be beginning next week.
sentences.zh: 它将于下周开始播出。

sentences.en: And if you want to hear all of the episodes detailing the Great Northern War and its aftermath,
sentences.zh: 如果你想收听所有详细讲述大北方战争及其后果的单集节目，

sentences.en: then you can sign up at therestofthishistory.com if you're not already a member of the club.
sentences.zh: 那么如果你还不是俱乐部的会员，可以在 therestofthishistory.com 注册。

sentences.en: And if you don't want to do that, then that's fine.
sentences.zh: 如果你不想这么做，那也没关系。

sentences.en: The episodes will be coming out in due course.
sentences.zh: 节目将会适时推出。

sentences.en: In the meanwhile, Dominic, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，多米尼克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Some wonderful stories and all that.
sentences.zh: 还有一些精彩的故事等等。

sentences.en: Beards, corsets, wheelbarrows, it's all been kicking off.
sentences.zh: 胡须、束腰外衣、独轮车，这下可全热闹起来了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And as we say, next week, the Great Northern War.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，下周，大北方战争。

sentences.en: So bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 那么，再见。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
